News.title: ‘Beautiful’ Brit girl, 3, who drowned in swimming pool on Majorca holiday pictured as heartbroken mum pays tribute
News.content:
POOL TRAGEDY ‘Beautiful’ Brit girl, 3, who drowned in swimming pool on Majorca holiday pictured as heartbroken mum pays tribute

A BRITISH three-year-old girl drowned on a family holiday to Majorca, an inquest heard today.

Eleri Ellesmere was on the trip with parents Joe and Cerys when she was found unresponsive in the swimming pool on June 24.



Desperate family members battled to save her at Villa Francisca before she was rushed to hospital.

Gwent Coroner’s Court in Wales heard Eleri tragically could not be saved and was declared dead the following day.



Her cause of death has been given as a 1a mechanical asphyxiation by drowning, respiratory failure.

Coroner Rose Farmer adjourned the hearing until April 13, 2027.

Paying tribute, Eleri’s heartbroken mum Cerys said: “What should have been an idyllic family holiday has turned into every parent’s worst nightmare. A nightmare we cannot wake up from.

“Our precious little Eleri Fairy was involved in an accident during the holiday.



“Unfortunately, despite unbelievable effort and attempts to heal our little girl made by us and the Palma health services, we were left with her on life sustaining support.

“Me and Joe were with her every single second and our little girl showed incomprehensible strength to try and stay with us. This was not enough.”

A fundraising page launched to help Eleri’s heartbroken family said her parents were facing an “unimaginable loss”.

It added: “Eleri was deeply loved, and her loss has left an unimaginable emptiness in all of our lives.

“No family should ever have to endure such pain, and yet we are now facing the most devastating chapter a mother, father and surrounding family can experience.



“We want to surround them with love, support, and care in every way possible.

“The funds raised will help ensure that beautiful Eleri is given the funeral she truly deserves- a farewell filled with dignity, love, and respect.”

News.title: Does the King have to swear in the new Prime Minister, and can Charles III call a General Election?
News.content:
As Sir Keir Starmer makes his Downing Street exit and Andy Burnham heads to Buckingham Palace, Britain witnesses its seventh Prime Minister in a decade take charge.

While political handovers at No10 move fast, centuries of constitutional tradition lie behind the palace doors.

From private audiences with King Charles III to official royal proclamations, the Monarch plays a crucial constitutional role in today’s transition.



Does the King ‘swear in’ a new Prime Minister?

Despite popular belief, King Charles III will not technically “swear in” Andy Burnham today.



In the UK political system, there is no public oath of office taken by the incoming PM outside No10 or in Parliament.

Instead, the official transfer of power occurs during a private audience at Buckingham Palace in an age-old process known as the “Kissing of Hands.”

Here’s how today’s transition at the Palace unfolds:



The resignation: Outgoing PM Keir Starmer travels to Buckingham Palace to formally tender his resignation to King Charles III.

Outgoing PM Keir Starmer travels to Buckingham Palace to formally tender his resignation to King Charles III. The audience: Minutes later, incoming Labour leader Andy Burnham arrives. The King invites him to form a government as he commands the majority in the House of Commons.

Minutes later, incoming Labour leader Andy Burnham arrives. The King invites him to form a government as he commands the majority in the House of Commons. The handshake: Despite the traditional term “Kissing of Hands,” no hands are actually kissed today. Burnham will bow, shake the King’s hand, and accept the royal commission.

The formal legal oaths – such as the Oath of Allegiance and Oath of Office – happen separately when cabinet ministers are appointed through the Privy Council, not during the King’s audience.

Could King Charles force a new General Election?

With another change at the top of government today, many wonder if the King could simply call a fresh General Election.

The short answer is no. Under the Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act 2022, the authority to trigger an early election rests with the PM, who requests that the Monarch dissolve Parliament.

While King Charles holds formal power under the Royal Prerogative to sign the official dissolution proclamation, constitutional convention dictates he acts strictly on the advice of his PM.



The Sovereign remains strictly politically neutral and cannot trigger a General Election on his own initiative.

In theory, under historic principles known as the Lascelles Principles, the King could say no to an election request.

He could only do this if Parliament was still working, and another politician had enough support from MPs to step up and run the country.

But in modern practice, if a PM requests a dissolution, the King grants it.

Could King Charles not accept Andy Burnham as PM?

The Monarch does not pick or choose who governs Britain based on personal preference.



The core rule of the UK constitution says the King must appoint whichever individual commands the confidence of the House of Commons.

For Andy Burnham to take office today, key constitutional criteria had to be fulfilled.

He returned to Parliament as an MP following his Makerfield by-election victory, before securing the leadership of the governing Labour Party.

Burnham also retains the backing of the majority of MPs in the House of Commons.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With those requirements met, King Charles has a constitutional duty to ask Burnham to form a government.



Refusing to appoint a democratically backed leader would spark a constitutional crisis and break the political neutrality of the Crown.

News.title: Horrifying moment wildfire rips through Spain as hundreds evacuated and tributes paid to ‘lovely’ Brit couple killed
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment an inferno rips through Spain, as a British couple are named among those killed in the wildfires.

Horrifying footage of the forest fire shows firefighters battling a wall of dancing flames as the Spanish countryside is transformed into a smouldering hellscape.



The footage emerged as Britons Christine and Michael Chard were named among the 13 people killed so far in the fires that have burnt across Spain, forcing hundreds to flee their homes.

The couple, who had moved to Bedar in Almeria province, were remembered as “lovely, lovely people” in tributes shared on a local Facebook page.



“So so sorry and sad to read this, lovely lovely people. I will always think of you Christine when listening to Motown,” one friend said on the page.



It comes as another blaze rages north of Madrid, that has forced about 700 residents to evacuate since it erupted on Thursday.



About 300 firefighters using 26 water-dropping aircraft are working to contain the blaze which has burned 32,000 acres of land in Guadalajara province.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said in a post on X that his government was closely monitoring the wildfire and thanked firefighters “working tirelessly” to protect lives.

“We are closely monitoring the situation regarding the Guadalajara fire, which has already scorched more than 13,000 hectares,” he said.

“I extend my full appreciation to those working tirelessly to protect lives and contain the blaze.”



The fire has been described as “difficult” to combat due to its location by the head of the regional government, Emiliano García-Page.

It broke out in a forest-covered mountainous area that includes the Sierra Norte Natural Park, which is home to endangered species including eagles, wolves and butterflies.

This summer has been one of Spain‘s most deadly for wildfires in recent years, with blazes also breaking out in other parts of Europe amid high summer temperatures.

Among the 13 killed during the recent wildfires are seven Britons, including Ian Jarvis, originally from Kent, and Pete and Fran Gillam, who were all expats living in Bedar.

Spain is expected to face another day of scorching weather, with temperatures due to reach 38C in Almeria and as high as 40C in Zaragoza.



The city in Spain’s Aragon region in the northwest has also been impacted by fires, with another blaze breaking out on Wednesday forcing people in nearby villages to evacuate.

Firefighters, aided by improved weather conditions, had managed to contain the fire’s spread, Aragon’s deputy regional president María del Mar Vaquero said on Spanish public television.

The fire has burned about 14,400 hectares, Ms Vaquero said.

News.title: Can I cut my neighbour’s tree branches if they overhang in my garden? Your legal rights explained
News.content:
WHEN it comes to maintaining your garden, your next door neighbour’s plants can feel like a nuisance.

If you keep your outdoor space tidy and trimmed, it’s easy to be tempted to chop away at greenery hanging over from your neighbour’s garden, too.



But there are some important rules you need to be aware of before you take your shears to branches crossing over your fence.

You do in fact have the right to trim branches that cross over into your garden, but only up to the boundary of your property line.



You must also return the cut off branches to your neighbour, unless they don’t want them.

According to the Royal Horticultural Society, cutting off overhanging branches can be done “provided it is done without trespassing onto the other person’s property”.



“It is also permissible to climb into the tree to undertake the work, again so long as it does not require going into the neighbour’s garden/land,” the RHS adds.

Permission is also not required to trim overhanging branches.

“Your actions are classed as ‘abating a nuisance’ which does not require permission. Only in situations where you need access to their land to undertake the work would permission be required,” the RHS says.

Once the branches have been pruned, they must be offered back to the neighbour.



The RHS advice explains: “If the owner doesn’t want them then you will be responsible for disposing of the prunings; you can’t simply throw them over the boundary into your neighbour’s garden!”

You are not allowed to pick and keep fruit from branches hanging over into your garden.

It’s important to note that “trees covered by a Tree Preservation Order (TPO) or in a Conservation Area will require prior consent from the local authority”.

Cutting a tree covered by a TPO can result in fines of up to £20,000. You can check if a tree is covered by contacting your council’s planning department.

News.title: Woman sexually assaulted in Wetherspoons pub in popular UK seaside town as cops release CCTV in hunt for man
News.content:
SEX ATTACK Woman sexually assaulted in Wetherspoons pub in popular UK seaside town as cops release CCTV in hunt for man

A WOMAN was allegedly sexually assaulted at a Wetherspoons pub – with cops now issuing a CCTV grab as part of their investigation.

They are looking to identify the man pictured following reports of the incident in Poole, Dorset, on July 11.



A man allegedly inappropriately touched a woman over her clothing while was at the bar at The Blackwater Stream in Lower Blandford Road, Broadstone, at around 8.30pm.

Police Constable Billy Edwards, of Poole police, said: “We have been carrying out detailed enquiries into this incident and I am now in a position to issue an image of a man we would like to identify as part of this investigation.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Dorset Police online or by calling 101, quoting occurrence number 55260070385.

Alternatively, independent charity Crimestoppers can be contacted anonymously online using its website or by calling Freephone 0800 555 111.

News.title: Starmer says ‘I go with grace’ & vows ‘full support’ for Burnham as he leaves No10 with wife & kids after 2 years as PM
News.content:
SIR Keir Starmer today “closed the book” on his time as Prime Minister as he gave Andy Burnham his “full support”.

The outgoing premier made a short goodbye speech of less than five minutes flanked by his wife Victoria and his closest political aides stood behind him.



But after two tumultuous years in Downing Street he said “my work is done” and said it had been the “privilege of my life”.

He will now formally resign to King Charles before Mr Burnham has his audience at Buckingham Palace shortly afterwards.



Mr Burnham will then be Britain’s seventh PM in a decade and set about appointing his first Cabinet.

Sir Keir said: “I go with a smile and I go proud of everything that we have achieved”.



He also praised the “resolve, grit, decency and compassion” of the British people, singling out members of the Armed Forces, NHS staff and volunteers.

But he used the speech to say that the UK’s enemies will “stop at nothing” to divide the UK especially as it stands behind the Ukraine in its fight against Russia.



He said: “We face a world now where our enemies will stop at nothing to divide us because of our values, our freedom, our decency and frankly because of our unflinching resolve towards the great people of Ukraine.

“And so under this attack, it is vital that we remember the greatness of the Britain all around us, that while we debate how to fix our problems, there is something we inherit from our country and our character that can give us confidence.

Read Sir Keir Starmer's farewell speech in full “I’m about to visit His Majesty the King to offer my resignation and close the book on my time as prime minister. “My work is done. In six-and-a-half years, I took our party from a historic defeat in 2019, changed it so it was fit to face the country, and won a landslide general election victory in 2024. “Since then, it has been the privilege of my life to serve you and this great country as prime minister, and I am confident that Britain is now stronger and fairer than it was two years ago. “Our economy is stronger; our public services are on the up, with the biggest fall in waiting times for 17 years; children are being lifted out of poverty every single day; immigration is down significantly; our defence and security are on a far stronger footing and our international reputation is greatly advanced. “Yet the thing I will always take away with me – the most humbling aspect of this job – is the front-row seat you get to witness the greatest things of this country in action, to see every day immeasurable acts of resolve, grit, decency, and compassion from people who serve our country, whether that’s in their regimental colours, NHS scrubs, or simply the millions of people in their communities who volunteer their time and their effort to the ground beneath their feet. “We face a world now where our enemies will stop at nothing to divide us because of our values, our freedom, our decency, and frankly, because of our unflinching resolve towards the brave people of Ukraine. “And so, under this attack, it is vital that we remember the greatness of the Britain all around us. That while we debate how to fix our problems, there is something we inherit from our country and our character that can give us confidence that we can change our country for the better, that we can create a Britain where every child can go as far as their talent will take them, and we can unite different people under our common flag if we don’t succumb to that division. “So, as I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham, I wish him every success. He has my full support. “And finally, I want to thank once again my family, Vic, and our children, my team, all the staff here and across the Labour Party, everyone at Number 10, and across the civil service, and everyone who has supported our efforts along the way. “For all the focus on individuals, politics will always be a team sport, and the changes we’ve delivered for our country and our party belong to everyone who has fought for them. “I thank them again today, and I thank the British people for the opportunity to serve. I go with good grace. I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved. “Thank you very much.”

“That we can change our country for the better, that we can create a Britain where every child will go as far as their talent will take them, and we can unite different people under our current flag if we don’t succumb to that division.”

His closest political allies watched on as he delivered his address on the steps of Downing Street.

Chancellor Rachel Reeves, expected to leave the Treasury, listened to his remarks along with Housing Secretary Steve Reed.



Also seen were Justice Secretary David Lammy and London Mayor Sir Sadiq Khan.

He used his speech to talk of the change he has made to the Labour Party after taking over following the devastating defeat at the 2019 election.

In a speech of less than five minutes, he said: “In six and a half years, I took our party from a historic defeat in 2019, changed it so it was fit to face the country, and won a landslide general election victory in 2024.

“Since then, it has been the privilege of my life to serve you and this great country as Prime Minister, and I am confident that Britain is now stronger and fairer than it was two years ago.”

News.title: Village ‘holding vote to leave the UK’ over plans to house more than 1,000 migrants on former military base
News.content:
LIVID locals in a tiny village have pledged to vote on leaving the UK amid fury over plans to house more than 1,000 migrants near their homes.

Some 350 residents of Piddington, Oxfordshire, are vowing to hold an independence referendum amid the “frightening” proposal.



Home Office plans would see 1,250 male asylum seekers – almost four times the local population – moved to a nearby ex-Ministry of Defence site.

Bicester Garrison has been chosen as part Labour’s wider scheme to convert MoD facilities into migrant housing and close asylum hotels.



But humans rights groups, the local council and MP Calum Miller have objected to the controversial plans for “Site A”.

And in a vote on July 4 – symbolic for American independence – 96 per cent of villagers said they wanted a referendum on leaving the UK.



Tim McNally, Piddington parish council chairman, told The Telegraph the local authority had been given “no prior warning” to the plans.

He said: “It’s about representation. We have had no input into the proposal. We have been asking questions, and nothing has come back.



“The shock of the information triggered people. I could have prepared them if I was given prior warning.

“George Washington brought change about. I am going to make the change and then give away the power like he did.”

There is no current legal mechanism allowing a village to declare independence from the UK.

And the unprecedented move could only happen with the agreement of the Government and Parliament.

But furious villagers say they have been driven to vote for the referendum in the wake of the “nightmare” plans.



Gwen McEwan described the prospect as “frightening” and vowed to stop paying council tax if the move went ahead.

She said: “Why should we suffer? There are people waiting for houses in this country, people on the breadline, and these people get handouts.

“We’ve got two buses, at 10 o’clock and 12 o’clock on weekdays – our children have to pay to get the bus to school, £300 a term.

“I’m not happy about it. They shouldn’t put them in a camp in a rural village. If they come here, I won’t be paying any council tax.”

Graham Rixon added: “It’s completely inappropriate.



“We’re a village of 350 people – there’s another village down the road of even less people, and they’re going to dump 1,200 people here.

“Most of them probably won’t speak the language, so there’s going to be communication problems.

“We haven’t had any detail of how it’s going to work, so if it does go through, it’ll be a mess – inadequate provision has been made.

“We’re supposed to live in a democracy, and this is just trying to bypass democracy and get it all done before anyone notices.”

Similar plans have sparked fury across the UK – with huge protests against the takeover of another army site in Crowborough, East Sussex.



Calum Miller, MP for Bicester and Woodstock, accused the Government of making “secret decisions” without consulting local authorities.

A Home Office spokesperson told The Sun the concerns of communities were “central to our immigration reforms”.

They added: “We are working with local authorities and others to fairly disperse asylum seekers across basic accommodation including ex-military sites.

“Three more military sites are being explored to house asylum seekers. We are seeing results.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The population of asylum seekers in hotels has fallen by 35% in the last year and by 63% from the peak under the previous government.



“Overall asylum costs have already fallen by £1 billion since this Government was elected.”

News.title: Polish national, 35, charged after ‘two teen girls raped and sexually assaulted on UK beach’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BEACH HORROR Polish national, 35, charged after ‘two teen girls raped and sexually assaulted on UK beach’

A POLISH national has been charged after two teen girls were allegedly raped and sexually assaulted on a UK beach.

Dawid Wlach was held following the horror on Great Yarmouth’s South Beach on May 16.



The 35-year-old is accused of two counts of rape and two counts of sexual assault.

Wlach appeared at Great Yarmouth Police Investigation Centre on Saturday.



He is the second man to be charged over the incident after Madalin Ilinca was also detained.

The Romanian national, 34, was arrested after being stopped at the Port of Dover re-entering Britain.

He appeared at Norwich Magistrates’ Court last month charged with the rape of a girl aged over 16.

He is also accused of two counts of sexual assault on a girl aged 16 or over.

Prosecutor Katherine Newson said the two teenage girls were “previously strangers to the defendant”.

She told the court both alleged victims had encountered another man, who had “fetched alcohol”.



The prosecutor added: “During this time, Ilinca approached the group. It is alleged he sexually assaulted one of the complainants at the rear of the hotel.

“All parties went onto the beach where the allegations of rape and sexual penetration occurred.”

Both men are due to appear at Norwich Crown Court for a hearing on July 28.

Police were called at 12:37am to reports two girls had been raped on sand dunes behind a Premier Inn.

The scene is also close to the Pleasure Beach amusement park and is overlooked by the Wellington Pier.

News.title: Brit girl, 3, dies in 'every parent's nightmare' tragedy on Mallorca holiday
News.content:
Brit girl, 3, dies in 'every parent's nightmare' tragedy on Mallorca holiday

Three-year-old Eleri Ellesmere was found unresponsive in a swimming pool at a villa in Mallorca before being rushed to hospital where she tragically died

View 4 Images Eleri Ellesmere was found unresponsive at a villa in Mallorca (Image: Gofundme)

A three-year-old girl tragically died after she was pulled from a swimming pool on a family holiday to Mallorca, an inquest heard today.

‌



Eleri Ellesmere was away with parents Joe and Cerys when the "tragic accident" unfolded on the evening of June 24. The family were staying at Villa Francisca, a rural home near Pollenca, during what "should have been an idyllic family holiday," they said.

‌



Eleri was pulled from the pool and family members performed CPR before she was taken to Son Espases Hospital in the capital city of Palma, an inquest opening heard.

‌



Despite the best efforts of medics, who the family say "battled tirelessly" to bring Eleri back, she was pronounced dead the following day, Gwent Coroner's Court was told.

View 4 Images Eleri was on holiday with her parents when she died (Image: Gofundme)

Eleri's provisional cause of death was given as 1a mechanical asphyxiation by drowning, respiratory failure. Coroner Rose Farmer opened and adjourned the hearing to April 13, 2027.

‌



The toddler, of New Tredegar, Gwent, was described as a "deeply loved" and "beautiful" little girl whose death left the family facing their "most devastating chapter," the inquest heard.

Eleri's heartbroken mum Cerys said: "What should have been an idyllic family holiday has turned into every parent's worst nightmare. A nightmare we cannot wake up from.

"Our precious little Eleri Fairy was involved in an accident during the holiday.

‌



View 4 Images The family said their holiday turned into 'every parent's worst nightmare' (Image: Gofundme)

"Unfortunately, despite unbelievable effort and attempts to heal our little girl made by us and the Palma health services, we were left with her on life sustaining support.

"Me and Joe were with her every single second and our little girl showed incomprehensible strength to try and stay with us. This was not enough."

‌



The family from Newport, South Wales, were devastated when Eleri's heart stopped beating at the Spanish hospital. Cerys said: "At 13:40 CEST on 25/06/2026 our fairy's heart stopped for the very last time.

"We are broken, we have no words. It is like the world has stopped and we have no breath. We want to thank every single member of the ambulance and hospital that battled tirelessly to try and bring our daughter back to us.

"Our only focus now is bringing our little girl back to the UK to be reunite her with her family." A fundraising page was launched to support the family with funeral costs.

‌



View 4 Images Eleri died in hospital on June 25 (Image: Gofundme)

It said: "As a family, we are coming together to raise funds for our cherished family members, the heartbroken parents of their beautiful daughter, Eleri Ellesmere.

"Eleri was deeply loved, and her loss has left an unimaginable emptiness in all of our lives.

‌



"No family should ever have to endure such pain, and yet we are now facing the most devastating chapter a mother, father and surrounding family can experience. We want to surround them with love, support, and care in every way possible.

"The funds raised will help ensure that beautiful Eleri is given the funeral she truly deserves- a farewell filled with dignity, love, and respect.

"They will also allow her parents the time and space to grieve without the added weight of financial worry, so they can focus on healing and leaning on one another during this heartbreaking time.

Article continues below

"Every donation, no matter how small, will help ease some of the burden they are carrying.

"Thank you for standing with our family during this time of unimaginable loss."

News.title: Europe weather maps show 50C heatwave as tourists in Spain face hottest day ever
News.content:
Europe weather maps show 50C heatwave as tourists in Spain face hottest day ever

Weather forecasting data suggests temperatures in Europe could hit 50C for the first time ever this month as Spain, Portugal and France face their hottest days in history

View 3 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures in Spain, France and Portugal will surge well above the seasonal average later this month (Image: WXCHARTS)

Heatwaves have ravaged Europe already this year, and weather models suggest the worst may be still to come before the end of this month.

‌



The UK is coming out of its third heatwave of the year, but temperatures are expected to rise again soon and bring a fourth scorching spell. And a similar pattern appears to be developing on the continent.

‌



GFS weather model data suggests tourists heading to parts of Portugal, Spain and France this month should be prepared to experience some never-before-seen temperatures, as each country could record its warmest ever day.

‌



The maps show temperatures in southern parts of Portugal could reach a staggering 50C on July 28 - which would be the hottest temperature ever recorded in Europe. The current European temperature record is 48.8C, registered near the city of Syracuse in Sicily on August 11, 2021.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 28 (Image: WXCHARTS)

European tourist hotspots face record-breaking weather and 48C heatwave in days READ MORE :

UK weather maps show most intense heatwave yet is coming as 15 counties hit 38C READ MORE :

The hottest temperature ever recorded in Portugal is currently 47.4C, which came on August 1, 2003 in Amareleja, a town in the region of Alentejo. Although coastal regions where most tourists will be heading in Portugal are set to be cooler, with possible 45C highs along the southern Atlantic coast - inland areas in the south could surpass 48C quite widely.

‌



Spain could also see its record temperature on July 28, with south-western areas potentially reaching 49C - including the tourist hotspot of Seville. The highest temperature ever recorded in Spain is 47.6C, which came on August 14, 2021 in La Rambla, Córdoba.

France’s current highest temperature ever recorded is 46C, which came in Verargues on June 28, 2019. The GFS model suggests several areas in the south and south-west could surpass this on July 31 with potential 47C highs just inland from the Atlantic coast, including in Bordeaux.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 31 (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



Temperature anomaly maps for the end of July show huge swathes of Portugal, France, Spain and Italy shaded in dark red and black. This indicates where temperatures are expected to rise well above the seasonal average.

Evacuations were ordered in central and north-eastern Spain over the weekend following major wildfires, one in the province of Guadalajara and another near Zaragoza. This follows devastating wildfires which ripped through southern parts of Spain earlier this month and claimed the lives of 13 people.

Professor Bill McGuire, Emeritus Professor of Geophysical & Climate Hazards at UCL, previously warned we could see 50C in Europe before the end of this year. He said: “It would be no surprise if 50C was exceeded, either later this summer or next year, when the heating impact of the unprecedented El Niño building in the Pacific will be at its greatest.”

Article continues below

He added that there was “no doubt whatsoever” climate change was driving the extreme heat, explaining: “Europe is heating faster than any other continent as we continue to add more than 40 billion tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere every year – equivalent to the weight of 800,000 Titanics.

“The average temperature of Europe is now more than 2C hotter than it was 100 years ago, and high temperature extremes are going up even faster. Heatwaves are getting hotter and longer, and taking many thousands of lives every year.”

News.title: Second man charged after two teen girls 'raped on Great Yarmouth beach'
News.content:
Second man charged after two teen girls 'raped on Great Yarmouth beach'

Norfolk Police said a second man, Dawid Wlach, has been charged after two teenage girls were allegedly raped and sexually assaulted on a beach in Great Yarmouth

View Image Two teenage girls were allegedly attacked on a beach in Great Yarmouth (file) (Image: visitgreatyarmouth.co.uk)

A second man has been charged after two teenage girls were allegedly raped and sexually assaulted on a beach in Great Yarmouth.

Norfolk Police said Dawid Wlach has been charged with two counts of rape and two counts of sexual assault after the incident at the seaside resort on May 16.

The force said the 35-year-old, of Caister-on-Sea, appeared at Great Yarmouth Police Investigation Centre on Saturday.

He is the second man charged in the case.

Madalin Ilinca, 34, of Great Yarmouth, appeared before Norwich Magistrates’ Court last month charged with one count of rape and two counts of sexual assault.

Article continues below

Police said the charges relate to reports that two teenage girls were sexually assaulted and raped on South Beach.

Ilinca has been remanded in custody while Wlach has been conditionally bailed.

The force said both men are due to appear at Norwich Crown Court for a hearing on July 28.

News.title: Man sliced and killed by boat propeller in Canary Islands as helpless friend watches
News.content:
Man sliced and killed by boat propeller in Canary Islands as helpless friend watches

A man aged in his 60s was killed after being sliced and caught up in the propeller of a pleasure boat off Puntagorda, La Palma, in the Canary Islands

View Image A man has died after being sliced by the propeller of a boat off La Palma (file) (Image: Bildagentur-online/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

A man aged in his 60s died after being sliced by the propeller of a pleasure boat in the Canary Islands on Sunday.

‌



A friend helplessly watched on during the horrific accident in which the Spanish man was killed after becoming trapped between the blades. It took rescue workers several hours to release his body.

‌



In addition to the work to recover the body, paramedics had to assist the skipper who suffered an anxiety attack after the accident.

‌



The man and his friend, the skipper, had gone out for a day of fishing in the waters off the west coast of La Palma, in the municipality of Puntagorda, the Civil Guard said.

UK airline issues ‘urgent’ plea as key flights cancelled READ MORE :

UK weather maps turn volcanic red for next 31C heatwave with 19 counties above 30C READ MORE :

The pair had regularly gone fishing together for decades in the area. The skipper, from Puntagorda, has been left traumatised after witnessing what happened.

‌



Emergency services rushed to the scene after receiving a report that a man had suffered serious injuries from the propeller of a boat. It is understood that he fell into the water and was struck before becoming entangled in the blades.

A helicopter was sent out as well as a rescue boat with police and paramedics, but nothing could be done to save the man. An investigation is now underway.

The recreational boat involved in the accident was towed to the Port of Tazacorte. The Civil Guard will be carrying out the probe with the help of firefighters from the La Laguna park, who have gone to the site and made a dive with underwater equipment.

Article continues below

The tragedy occurred in a stretch of sea between Porís de Tijarafe and El Puerto de Puntagorda - an area that is commonly used for fishing and which can only be reached by boat, since a large part of the coastal strip of Puntagorda is made up of cliffs.

Many boats are based in the port of Tazacorte, like the vessel in this case, and they visit places such as Cueva Bonita or El Porís de Tijarafe among others.

The mayor of Puntagorda, Vicente Rodríguez Lorenzo, described the events as "an absolute tragedy" involving two men who were lifelong friends.

News.title: Your legal rights if your neighbour's hedge starts growing into your garden
News.content:
Your legal rights if your neighbour's hedge starts growing into your garden

Before you reach for the secateurs, here's what UK law actually allows you to do — and what could land you in serious legal trouble.

View 3 Images An overgrown hedge can ruin the look of your garden (Image: Witthaya Prasongsin via Getty Images)

No matter how well you get on with your neighbours, there are certain things that are always likely to cause a bit of tension. Failing to keep up with the gardening is a major one, especially where hedges are concerned.

‌



If you're someone who prides themselves in having a neat, tidy garden, there's nothing worse than when a neighbour doesn't quite have that same inclination.

‌



Spotting their hedge start to creep into your garden is enough to make anyone reach for the shears, but before you do, it's worth taking note of what you're legally allowed to do - and what might count as criminal damage.

‌



View 3 Images You are allowed to cut up until the boundary line (Image: Getty)

Can I cut my neighbour's hedge?

According to the official government website, you're entitled to cut back your neighbour's hedge if it overhangs into your property from their home or a public highway - but only under certain conditions.

You're only allowed to trim back to the property boundary, and your neighbour can actually take legal action if you exceed this.

‌



Your neighbour has an obligation to make sure their hedges don't harm your property or become excessively high, so if any damage arises your neighbour may be found liable.

As well as this, you might be banned from cutting any foliage if you live in a conservation area, or the trees in the hedge are protected by a tree preservation order, so it's worth checking with your local council before doing anything.

Who owns the hedge?

Before you start to cut the hedge, you must first work out who actually owns it. The experts at Grasslands Nursery said: "Ownership usually comes down to your property deeds. A hedge growing just inside one boundary belongs to that owner; a hedge planted along the line itself may be jointly owned.

‌



"Many deeds use a ‘T mark’ to show which side is responsible for a boundary — a T on your side means it is yours to maintain. If it is unclear, it is often treated as a shared responsibility, and a friendly conversation beats a formal dispute every time."

View 3 Images Hedges are a common cause of neighbourly disputes (Image: Cavan Images / Oscar Bjarnason via Getty Images)

How high can a hedge legally be?

While there are laws around how high fences and garden walls can generally be, there isn't a strict rule when it comes to hedges. According to Above All Tree Care, your neighbour’s hedge can legally grow to any height on their own property, but restrictions apply when it affects your 'reasonable enjoyment' of your home.

‌



The two-metre rule is more of a general guideline rather than a legal limit.

Local councils can check complaints about hedge heights based on several factors including the hedge’s impact on natural light, the affected property’s use, and whether the hedge serves a purpose.

The legislation targets evergreen hedges that form barriers, rather than individual trees or mixed plantings.

‌



What happens if you cut a hedge illegally?

If any cutting take place on your side of the boundary, this may constitute an offence under the Criminal Damage Act 1971, unless there's a lawful justification.

You're entitled to pursue a civil claim for any damage caused, although it's always recommended to try speaking with your neighbour first.

If approaching them directly seems intimidating, think about writing a letter that sets out the problem clearly while sticking firmly to the facts.

News.title: Aldi's new £25 gadget makes feeding babies 'easier' and 'NHS-approved'
News.content:
Aldi's new £25 gadget makes feeding babies 'easier' and 'NHS-approved'

The deal is arriving in all stores from Thursday, July 23

View 3 Images Aldi's latest Baby Event sale includes this £25 kit (Image: Peter Dazeley/Getty Images)

Parents will be able to shop for new baby products in an upcoming sale at Aldi. The sale will include a discounted gadget that could make a world of difference when little ones demand to be fed. The Rapid Cool Duo Pack will be available in the middle aisle at Aldi later this week.

‌



The bundle, costing £24.99, claims to make baby bottles the perfect temperature "in minutes". Aldi says that having the portable device on hand could help to reduce fussing and keep newborns and babies from waiting any longer than needed for their next feed.

‌



Describing the set online, Aldi said: "The Nuby Rapid Cool twin pack is travel-friendly, fitting into most changing bags with ease and requires no power supply. Ideal whether you’re feeding during the day or the night."

‌



Rapid Cool claims to be "super quick" as it creates the "perfect temperature" formula milk in only two minutes "without a sound". Aldi adds that the handheld device uses freshly boiled water to prepare bottle feeds "as per the NHS guidelines".

From Thursday, July 23, shoppers will have a choice of three styles when picking up this gadget, including blue, pink, or neutral designs. Aldi adds that these cooling kits are "easy to set up and clean" and that "no replacement filters are required".

View 3 Images Rapid Cool claims to be "super quick" at bringing formula down to the "perfect temperature" (Image: Aldi)

‌



The deal arrives in stores across the UK as part of Aldi's latest Baby Event. The sale includes items like toys, clothes and feeding accessories from £1.99 as well as stand-out SpecialBuys like safety gates (£17.99), a bedside crib (£49.99) and a 360° Car Seat (£89.99).

Aldi regularly rotates the items in its middle aisles every Thursday and Sunday. Although the items may seem random to the average shopper in the store, the supermarket follows a clear set of themes each week.

People who often shop at the budget supermarket may be interested to know they can stay ahead of the deals before they land in store by picking up one of the physical in-store leaflets after they check out. Alternatively, look online here for upcoming offers.

How the NHS says parents should make formula bottles

The NHS website lists a step-by-step method that parents can use to make the safest bottles for their newborns. The device has its own guide to follow that keeps all of this in mind, without overcomplicating the process for families.

News.title: Chris Mason: Burnham is fifth PM in four years - now he'll try to buck the trend
News.content:
By lunchtime today, the UK will have its fifth prime minister in four years.

No other sentence can so pithily summarise the nature of British politics right now than that one.

In the summer of 2022 Boris Johnson was on his way out, but still in office. Since then there has been Liz Truss, Rishi Sunak and Sir Keir Starmer.

Little wonder Andy Burnham will say later, we are told, that he is "acutely conscious" of this churn at the top. His critics, within the Labour Party and beyond it, may allow themselves a wry smile at that, given they would argue he has been agitating for this moment for ages.

In the post-pandemic, post-Brexit 2020s, when for so long so many have felt like life is getting harder, the national mood is impatient and political support is fragmenting.

The consequence of that in recent years has meant those in government have been unpopular.

That is the backdrop to Burnham's arrival in Downing Street, just as it was for Sir Keir Starmer 746 days ago - on another sunny July day, just two years back.

That trend of unpopular governments is the thing Burnham is now trying to buck.

He is determined to hit the ground running and, where possible, to maintain the style of leadership he adopted as the mayor of Greater Manchester.

The rules of the House of Commons and meetings with the King, among others, will probably mean he wears a suit more often than he has in recent years.

But other conventions may be very intentionally ditched. I hear, for instance, that he may not bother with a lectern for his first speech as prime minister, outside 10 Downing Street, on Monday.

I also hear he is keen on question and answer sessions with voters around the country - "People's Question Time" as one ally put it.

Before Burnham's big moment will come Sir Keir's departure.

News.title: A very quick guide to Andy Burnham
News.content:
Andy Burnham has been fairly tight-lipped about his plans for specific policies, but here's some of what we know:

Cost of living: After becoming prime minister, Burnham is expected to lay out plans to give "people breathing space on the cost of living".

Digital ID: Burnham will scrap plans for a government-issued digital ID for all British adults, in an attempt to shift focus to "the daily priorities facing people across the country, according to his office.

North Sea oil: The new prime minister will also announce plans for new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea. This is likely to only support existing licences rather than issuing new ones, BBC News understands.

Thames Water: Burnham has previously said he wants to see "greater public control" of water and energy sectors but has stopped short of calling for full nationalisation. Lenders to Thames Water are preparing to challenge any attempts to nationalise the country's biggest water company.

Taxes: Burnham has said there is "some room" for movement on tax. In an interview with LBC, he suggested business rates on warehouses could be increased to fund tax cuts for pubs and some high-street businesses. But he has said he would stick to pledges Labour made not to raise VAT, income tax or National Insurance in its general election manifesto in 2024. He has not ruled out a wealth tax.

Local power: A key priority will be to hand more power to councils and authorities away from Parliament. That would involve giving them more control in areas such as housing and transport. As part of that he wants to create another No 10 team over 150 miles north of London, based in Manchester.

News.title: Watch: Sir Keir Starmer's last speech as prime minister in full
News.content:
Sir Keir Starmer has delivered his final address as prime minister on Monday as Andy Burnham takes the country's top job.

In front of an applauding crowd, Starmer said "my work is done" and wished Burnham well.

After repeated assurances he would hold on to the post, Starmer announced he would step down on 22 June - four days after Burnham won a Westminster seat.

Andy Burnham follows Keir Starmer, Rishi Sunak and Liz Truss.

Follow the story live.

News.title: Who is Andy Burnham's wife, Marie-France van Heel?
News.content:
She was described as the coolest girl in college when she first started dating Andy Burnham.

More than three decades later, Marie-France van Heel is about to walk into Downing Street alongside her husband to take on one of the most powerful unofficial roles in government - the prime minister's spouse.

Burnham will replace Sir Keir Starmer in No 10 on Monday, and he met Dutch-born van Heel, known as Frankie, when she started studying at Fitzwilliam College at the University of Cambridge in 1989.

He was in his second year of an English Literature degree, and Burnham's former lecturer, John Mullan, wrote in the Times that other students thought he had scooped the pools when they began dating.

News.title: Victory for football? Spain beat Argentina to win World Cup
News.content:
Describing a result as a 'victory for football' might seem like a trite cliche - but you won't find many neutrals disagreeing with that description of Spain's win in the 2026 World Cup final.

When Ferran Torres slammed in the extra-time winner, and Rodri lifted the trophy high in New Jersey, it is hard to imagine many will have had sympathy for Argentina.

Spain triumphed in a battle of endurance, for players and spectators, to beat the Argentines and win their second men's World Cup.

On every football metric - and, some would say, morality too - this was the right result.

"There is no doubt that the right team won," former England captain Alan Shearer said on BBC One. "From start to finish, Spain controlled possession. They were the ones looking to play football, create chances and get in behind.

"This is a result for football because of the way that they have played. Spain deserve it."

Spain had 65% possession, an expected goals tally of 1.94 and 20 shots on goal - 11 on target.

At the other end, goalkeeper Unai Simon kept his seventh clean sheet in eight matches as he won the Golden Glove for the tournament's best goalkeeper.

Spain conceded just one goal at the 2026 World Cup - the fewest conceded by any winning team.

News.title: Broadcaster and journalist Edward Stourton dies aged 68
News.content:
Broadcaster and journalist Edward Stourton, whose career spanned more than 40 years including a decade on Radio 4's Today, has died aged 68.

Stourton, who had been diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2014, died on Saturday surrounded by his family, the BBC announced in a statement.

The presenter's friend and former Today co-host James Naughtie praised Stourton's "warm intelligence and wit", adding he was "one of the best colleagues".

Another former Today presenter, Evan Davis, said Stourton was "a very important figure for all of us on the daily news programmes on Radio 4".

"One of those people you're really glad to have around," Davis continued. "All substance, minimum ego, deeply knowledgeable, totally reliable.

"And he was one of the nicest of colleagues as well. He'll be missed."

Presenter Mishal Husain remembered Stourton as "a true gentleman and a broadcaster of immense capacity and intellect".

News.title: Fire crews battle blaze on Arthur’s Seat in Edinburgh
News.content:
Fire crews have spent the night battling a large blaze on Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh.

Small plumes of smoke could still be seen on Monday morning along Salisbury Crags after the fire broke out the previous evening.

Six fire engines were sent to tackle the grassfire with firefighters seen dousing the flames.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said there were "no reported casualties" but Police Scotland said Queen's Drive, the road that encircles the Holyrood Park hills, remained closed to all vehicles.

It is the second fire in the last three months at the landmark, an ancient extinct volcano that offers panoramic views of the Scottish capital.

Edinburgh University student Mahek Jayantilial, who lives near Arthur's Seat, said she could see the fire from her window.

"I was a bit worried because I thought the fire would come this way, but thankfully there's enough concrete here to stop it," the 24-year-old told the Press Association.

News.title: My fitness tracker knew I was pregnant before I did
News.content:
Dr Stuart Lavery, consultant of reproductive medicine at University College Hospital in London, said: "People are understandably using this technology to try to get a greater understanding, and to try and pick up things as early as possible because it has such a profound impact on your life if you're planning a pregnancy."

However, "we might be running before we can walk," he cautioned.

"We probably need a lot more data on the reliability, we need a lot more researchâ¦ otherwise what happens is your levels of anxiety will just skyrocket," he said.

"I have no doubt that more people will be using technology, an app-based approach or a wearable-based approach, to try and pick up these things. But I think it should come with quite a big health warning about how much we can rely on them for accuracy."

When asked about the anxiety women reported feeling early in their pregnancy as a result of checking their ring data, Dr Chris Curry, Oura's clinical director of women's health, told BBC News: "With or without biometric tracking, pregnancy can be an uncertain time where many women, particularly those pregnant for the first time, are in the dark about the range of what's normal."

She added that if women feel overwhelmed, the company "encourages members to take a break from the app experience, whilst Oura Ring continues to collect data and gather insights", adding: "The ring is a support tool, not a replacement for your care team."

Ravika sadly did miscarry. She's hoping to start trying to conceive again soon - and when she does, her experience has made her rethink wearing her tracker again.

"I didn't really see myself as being an anxious person, butâ¦ I think going forward if it came to a point where I had an inkling that I was pregnant and my stats were low, as soon as that positive pregnancy test was there, I do think it would be the best thing for me to take the ring off."

News.title: Prisons minister Lord Timpson quits government
News.content:
The prisons minister has resigned from the government, the BBC has been told.

Lord James Timpson was appointed to the role in July 2024 after leaving his job as CEO of the Timpson group, a business which provides key cutting and shoe repair services and employs hundreds of former prisoners.

His arrival in government was greeted with much fanfare by some in the Labour Party and described as "radical" and "innovative".

But in a departing statement on Monday, seen exclusively by the BBC, Lord Timpson said he was stepping down and it was an "honour" to serve in the post.

His statement did not give a specific reason for resigning, but it is understood he feels he has done as much as he can in the role.

Prisons in England and Wales were at crisis point, reaching almost full capacity, when he first entered Sir Keir Starmer's government.

He oversaw the controversial early release scheme which saw tens of thousands of inmates let out to create more space in jails.

His critics will argue prisons continue to be violent, drug infused and overcrowded, while probation officers still report being overworked and unable to cope.

But figures do show assaults against staff and self-harm in prisons are falling.

Lord Timpson said in his resignation statement that he had left "our prisons and probation service in a much healthier and happier state than two years ago".

He added: "I'm proud to have become the longest-serving minister in this role for 15 years. I'm also proud that 75% of prisons and 90% of probation teams are now performing better than when I started.

"Self-harm, violence and assaults on staff are all down, and fewer people are leaving prison without a home to go to, a measure of dignity I care about deeply."

He also pointed to the Women's Justice Board he established, saying he "believe[s] most women should not be in prison at all" and "diverting them away from custody, helping them with often chaotic, damaged, and addicted lives, is one of the changes I'm proud to have achieved".

His critics may question why he is leaving before the Sentencing Act 2026 is enacted in September, when more people are expected to be released early and further criminals will serve their sentences in the community.

A source in the Ministry of Justice told the BBC: "We're gutted he's going but the new person is going to have their work cut out to get their head round what's round the corner."

News.title: Ryanair profits drop as Iran war puts off passengers and lifts fuel costs
News.content:
Ryanair's profits have fallen sharply as war in the Middle East sent jet fuel prices soaring and customers reluctant to book flights.

The Irish airline's pre-tax profits dropped 34% to â¬593m (Â£503m) between April and June while sales were flat as the company was forced to cut fares to stimulate demand.

Ryanair also said it expects summer fares to be slightly lower than last year due to "consumer hesitancy" around air travel.

The price of fuelling a plane has jumped since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February and while Ryanair said it had "hedged" or struck deals for the most future fuel costs, those not included in these arrangements had more than doubled.

Crude oil prices hit $90 (Â£67) a barrel for the first time in a month on Monday, before falling back slightly, after a weekend of intense exchanges of fire between the US and Iran.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz â an essential route for global oil and gas supplies â has ground to a halt.

An interim peace deal last month brought some respite to oil and energy prices, but they spiked again as negotiations broke down and fighting resumed.

The airline warned that its results for the year will be "highly sensitive" to external factors such as conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine as well as the price of unhedged jet fuel.

Fares for for the key summer period between July and September are on track to be "modestly" lower than last year, with many passengers booking closer to departure than normal.

The firm's finance chief, Neil Sorahan, said flights on its popular Mediterranean routes were still full. "People [are] as keen to get away as ever, albeit booking just a little bit later," he said.

Between April and June, Ryanair's revenue ticked up 1% to â¬4.4bn.

While passenger numbers rose 6% to 6.1 million- helped by the Easter holiday in April - fares fell by 6% as the airline reduced fares to entice flyers concerned about the Iran war.

Ryanair's share price fell 5% on Monday.

Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said Ryanair was in a better position than many of its rivals, but nonetheless "visibility is worse than San Francisco airport when the fog sets in".

"The renewed escalation in hostilities in the Middle East is unhelpful and without a lasting resolution, challenging times for the airline and travel space look set to continue."

News.title: Drug dealer exploited 14-year-old boy into selling drugs for him
News.content:
Siddiqi met the boy in Glasgow's St Enoch Centre during the school summer holidays in 2025 and asked if he "wanted to start making money".

The boy initially refused as he believed the dealer was talking about drugs.

But the High Court in Glasgow heard Siddiqi eventually persuaded the child to team up with him by suggesting he could use the cash to help his mother.

The youngster was given Siddiqi's Instagram account and later a mobile phone.

The boy lied to his mum that he had a "summer holiday camp" to go to after Siddiqi messaged him, and in mid-July the teenager was taken to a known drug den in Glasgow.

He ended up staying there for a number of days and was shown how to "bag up" crack cocaine.

Prosecutor Jennifer Nicholson-White said: "Siddiqi would attend the flat for only a couple of hours each day due to having an electronic tag. He would give the boy Â£20 to buy food."

The child was then taken by taxi to a dirty, rubbish-strewn property in Paisley in Renfrewshire.

He was told to hand out "testers" to local addicts - small samples of cocaine.

The boy ended up staying at the flat for the rest of the week.

The prosecutor said the child handed out about 60 testers and was given the phone numbers of drug users.

She added: "He estimated Siddiqi made about Â£700 each day in sales."

News.title: Residents told to pay £7,000 each to fix water pipe outside their homes
News.content:
Residents say they could face prosecution if they do not pay thousands of pounds to repair a water pipe outside their homes.

The residents of five houses in Pontycymer, Bridgend county, said they were told by Welsh Water that a leak from the shared pipe supplying their homes needs to be repaired at their own cost, which they estimate could cost more than Â£7,000 each.

The Garw Valley locals claim they have been given no evidence of where the leak is which their insurance companies need to cover the cost, causing sleepless nights.

A Welsh Water spokesperson said it does not own or manage the pipe so it's the responsibility of property owners, and residents have 11 days to fix it.

Welsh Water added that the leak needed to be repaired as it was wasting water, and it could issue a potential prosecution under Section 75 Notice under the Water Industry Act 1991, external.

The estimated cost of more than Â£7,000 would go towards replacing the rear water pipe in their back gardens with a new pipe at the front of the terraced row, they said, along with connecting it to each house individually.

Resident Nerys Walters said the dispute had brought her massive amounts of stress over the last two years.

She said they initially thought the cost of repairs could be covered through insurance, but with no evidence of the leak being provided, insurers have said they would not pay out.

Walters said: "It's been a nightmare situation for us that has really caused us all a lot of stress.

"Welsh Water have said they would pay for a new line that runs parallel to the front of the property, but we would then have to fund the cost of it coming in from the gate, and through the house to our rear stopcock.

Walters said she had spoken to "numerous contractors" who quoted the residents more than Â£1,000 a metre for the work.

"This has been going on for about a year and a half now and we've been asking for that evidence ever since but have been given nothing", she said.

"No evidence of the leak, and no reason as to why they adopted other pipes in the street but not ours. All the while the deadline they have given runs down. It's been very difficult and we just want to get it sorted."

News.title: Going with the flow: Renewable energy battery breakthrough
News.content:
A 3D-printed battery developed at Queen's University Belfast could "make a genuine impact" on the road to net zero, say the researchers behind it.

Flow batteries are seen as key to scaling up renewable energy, allowing it to be stored for when the wind is not blowing and the sun is not shining.

But they are expensive and typically use a metallic element - vanadium - that is only produced in a few places round the world.

Now, scientists at QUB have developed one based on iron, which is much easier to source, and have sent it around the world to help standardise research.

It is hoped it will accelerate the renewable energy revolution, making research more reliable and its findings more scalable.

News.title: 'I'm petrified my rapist could be released early'
News.content:
When Jade Belgrove finally saw the jailing of the man who raped her as a child, she thought her fight was over.

After waiting a decade to report the abuse she suffered as a 14-year-old, she believed justice had finally been served when Simon Tyler was jailed for nine years in 2024.

Now, after being told her attacker could be released years early under government plans to ease prison overcrowding, the 30-year-old from Coventry - who spoke to the BBC having waived her right to anonymity - said victims were being "let down all over again".

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it understood "the distress victims will feel" but added prisons could run out of spaces in November "without this action".

News.title: 'No more families should endure this' - parents of student who died from MenB back new vaccine advice
News.content:
The parents of a university student who died from meningitis B (MenB) say new vaccine advice represents a "poignant moment" and will save countless lives.

Helen and Lee Draper from Pontypool, Torfaen, lost their 18-year-old daughter Meg to the disease in October 2025, just weeks after she started at the University of Bournemouth.

Last week, official advice changed, telling governments they should offer a free jab from age 15 - despite previously saying this was not cost effective.

The Welsh government said implementation took time and it must consider affordability, feasibility and the effect on the wider NHS.

News.title: The 1975's Matty Healy marries model Gabbriette Bechtel in Los Angeles
News.content:
The 1975's frontman Matty Healy and model Gabriette Bechtel have tied the knot in Los Angeles.

The couple announced their engagement in 2024, after dating for nine months, and got married on Saturday.

A statement shared from the couple's representatives said the pair were married "at a private ceremony in Los Angeles, attended by their family and close friends".

According to several US media outlets, they were married at Madonna's former estate in the Hollywood Hills and celebrities including Charli XCX were in attendance.

Bechtel, 28 and Healy, 37 were first linked months after he split from Taylor Swift, whom he dated briefly in 2023. Their relationship reportedly inspired some of the tracks on Swift's acclaimed album, The Tortured Poets Department.

In June 2024, Bechtel shared a photo of her wearing a large black diamond ring on her ring finger on Instagram.

She wrote: "Marrying The 1975 is very brat."

Healy's mother, Loose Women star Denise Welch, later confirmed the engagement on a podcast.

Videos of Healy reportedly at his stag-do performing with The 9075 - a tribute band to The 1975 - have also been circulating online.

Bechtel also shared photos from her Las Vegas hen-do, showing the model being handcuffed and carried onto a plane by a man dressed as a police officer.

Other snaps showed fake 100 dollar bills spread across the floor, her posing with burlesque star Dita Von Teese, and dancing with an Elvis impersonator.

The American model is also a musician, known for being the lead vocalist and songwriter of the punk rock band Nasty Cherry, which was formed by Charli XCX. Her husband, George Daniel, is The 1975's drummer.

The 1975 are known for their songs Chocolate, Somebody Else, and Girls and have had five UK number one albums including their 2013 self-titled debut, 2020's Notes On A Conditional Form and their most recent album, Being Funny In A Foreign Language, which was released in 2022.

They also headlined Glastonbury last year. The band have since gone on an "indefinite hiatus" from performing live shows.

The BBC has contacted Healy and Bechtel for comment.

News.title: Andy Burnham’s father unaware of son becoming prime minister due to Alzheimer’s
News.content:

Andy Burnham’s father Roy, who has Alzheimer’s, does not know that his son will become the next prime minister.

Mr Burnham told The Times that his father is unaware that he will take office on Monday.

“That’s a sadness because he would be [proud],” the incoming prime minister said.

“The way I look at it, it’s his achievement as well. A whole family achievement although he doesn’t know it.”

Mr Burnham has vowed to “grasp the nettle” of reforming the adult social care system, drawing on his father’s experience.

He said that his father was also unaware that Mr Burnham had swung behind a change in the voting system to proportional representation, which was one of Roy’s political passions.

He said: “I don’t think he’s ever realised, because of his condition, that I’ve come round to PR, which is one of his missions – to get me to accept that.”

Mr Burnham said that the family, including his youngest daughter, visited his father last Sunday.

“We were at his care home. My two brothers were there, my mum was there. So, all five of us together, which was a nice thing.”

Reform of the social care system is unfinished business for Mr Burnham, who set out plans for change while he was health secretary in Gordon Brown’s administration.

open image in gallery Burnham hugging his parents Eileen and Roy after he was selected as Labour’s candidate for the Greater Manchester mayor role ( PA )

Mr Burnham described the “broken social care system” in England as “the worst of all worlds” and said that it is a “massive” priority for the public.

The PM-in-waiting, who will take up his role in Number 10 on Monday, acknowledged that reform will “require something difficult”, after his efforts to do so more than a decade ago failed.

His plans in 2010 to overhaul social care for the elderly with the creation of a national care service for England were turned against Labour by the Conservatives, who claimed that they would levy a “death tax” to pay for it.

“The minute that poster landed with the gravestones, that was it. My reforms were dead,” Mr Burnham later admitted.

Now he has pledged to “expend political capital” during his premiership on what he said has been a long-neglected sector – accusing Westminster of having “flinched” from such big decisions for too long.

Name-checking the issue in his first speech after formally replacing Sir Keir Starmer as Labour leader, he told a special conference in London on Friday: “Let’s take a problem-solving rather than a point-scoring approach.

open image in gallery The press gathers outside No 10 ahead of Andy Burnham being confirmed as the new prime minister ( PA )

“Let’s have the courage to fix the big things that politics has neglected, like social care, and have the conviction to go out there together and argue for our plans.”

How adult social care works and is funded in England has been a thorny issue for many governments over the years.

Unlike NHS care, social care is not free at the point of use and high costs sometimes mean people are forced to sell their homes to pay for what they need.

People with savings worth more than £23,250 are not entitled to help with the cost of care from their local council.

Baroness Louise Casey, who is leading an independent review into the sector and is expected to publish her first report later this year, noted in a speech earlier this month that there have been no fewer than 22 attempts since 1997 at reforming the sector – none of which she said had “fixed the foundations”.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has pledged to ‘grasp the nettle’ of adult social care ( PA )

In 2019, in his first speech as prime minister, Boris Johnson said the Conservatives would “fix the crisis in social care once and for all”, something that failed to come to fruition.

Labour faced criticism after the party was elected in 2024 for scrapping plans for an £86,000 cap on the amount anyone in England would need to spend on their personal care over their lifetime, having argued the proposals were not “deliverable” in the time frame.

After becoming Labour leader on Friday Mr Burnham referred to his family’s own experience of the system due to his father living with Alzheimer’s.

“I think it’s about being prepared to grasp the nettle,” he said.

“I’ve got personal experience of the system. My dad has Alzheimer’s and you see what the staff have to put up with. It’s not their fault. The system’s broken.

“You can’t leave social care like this.”

He said that while reform “will require something difficult” he believes the public want a better system.

He added: “The NHS won’t get back to where it needs to be when you have a broken social care system that can’t keep people out of hospital.

open image in gallery Former prime minister Boris Johnson pledged to ‘fix the crisis’ in social care ( PA )

“So this is massive when it comes to the things that people care about.

“And I’m not going to do what Westminster has traditionally done, which is to kick the can down the road on this important issue.

“I will expend political capital on bringing forward a plan to fix social care, and I’m not going to waste time because every time that we waste another year, thousands and thousands more people don’t get the care that they need.”

He said that with the system as it is, people are “paying for care in the most unfair way possible”, likening it to “the American healthcare system”.

Mr Burnham said: “The more vulnerable you are, the more you end up paying, so that’s the worst of all worlds and people lose everything that they’ve worked for.

“So you start from there and then you look at the options as to how you make a universal social care system, because that’s what I believe, a national care service, how do you fund that? And we’ll come to those options in due course.”

Speaking in May, before he became an MP, Mr Burnham said he did not “resile” from previous comments he had made about abolishing inheritance tax in favour of a care levy.

As the final whistle blew in New Jersey, Spain secured a World Cup triumph that briefly felt so inevitable, despite being almost two decades in the making.

16 years after winning their first World Cup, La Roja have a second star above their crest, courtesy of an infallible performance from Luis de la Fuente’s side in the 1-0 win over Argentina.

open image in gallery De la Fuente saw his side play a near-perfect game as they beat Argentina in the World Cup final ( Getty )

It was a scoreline that flattered the Albiceleste, despite the fact that Spain did not create as many chances as they could have given their dominance of the ball.

Argentina were poor on the whole, with even the genius of Lionel Messi unable to save them this time as a timid, abject performance played right into Spain’s hands.

Argentina could barely keep the ball, with their midfield and attack largely anonymous as Spain began to dominate. While the defence held firm during normal time, the attack was almost non-existent as the holders became the first team to ever have no shots after 90 minutes of a World Cup final.

In the end, Enzo Fernandez’s ridiculous red card proved their undoing, and Spain needed no invitation from there. Rodri, Pedri and Nico Williams were particularly impressive, and the winger ombined with Ferran Torres to win it, his cushioned header setting up the Barcelona forward to rifle in an accomplished half-volley in extra time.

It was no more than Spain deserved, while Argentina’s anti-football performance also got its just desserts. But while Argentina were undeniably poor, this was more than just an off-day for one team. Rather, it was also an imperious display from a side that have proved themselves the best in the world in recent years.

Spain’s triumphant Euro 2024 campaign was similar to this World Cup, La Roja growing into the tournament before a brilliant display in the semi-final against France marked them out as clear favourites. These displays were partly down to having an exceptionally talented group of players, but they were also made possible by a clear footballing idea provided by an equally as gifted manager.

open image in gallery Spain’s win gives them their second World Cup trophy in their history ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Spain were dominant from the early stages as they completely nullified any Argentina threat ( Reuters )

Of course, this is not a new idea. After the Euro 2024 campaign, De la Fuente spoke of having built “a team that was recognisably Spain”. Tiki-taka as we knew it was no more, but the manager – who had previously managed Spain teams at junior levels – had tinkered with it to develop his own brand. Tiki-taka 2.0, perhaps.

Spain’s dizzying ability to keep the ball is still a hallmark of their way of playing, and it was on show throughout the 120 minutes of Sunday’s final. The skill and composure of Aymeric Laporte and Pau Cubarsi is pivotal to a team who insist on playing the ball out from the back, while the role of the full-backs to serve as extra men in the final third, to “join from deeper lines” when necessary.

That was on show when Porro grabbed an impressive second in the win over France, and it could be seen today as himself and Cucurella operated in both wide and more central areas in the final third, with Porro picking up the ball inside the winger before delivering the cross that led to Torres’ goal. Rodri is the man tasked with keeping things ticking in the middle, but this is a Spain side who like to be more direct when possible.

In Dani Olmo, they have a capable attack-minded midfielder for more central areas, while Lamine Yamal is the obvious focal point on the wing. While he was unusually quiet in New Jersey, it only needs one moment to make it count. De la Fuente has previously spoken about “generating overloads in different areas of the pitch”, and Yamal and Porro did this repeatedly throughout, eventually leading to the winner.

open image in gallery Nico Williams helped change the game and was unlucky to see a goal disallowed for a foul in the build-up ( Reuters )

At the same time, Alex Baena had struggled on the other wing and De la Fuente eventually decided to introduce Nico Williams as he returned to an even more direct way of playing. The Bilbao man also helped change the game, almost opening the scoring himself and seeing a goal disallowed before grabbing the assist for Torres.

It was an attacking display that showed that Spain can hurt teams “with possession, with positional attacks built with many passes”, but while they impressed with the ball at their feet, the win over Argentina was also notable for their defensive display, and indeed how it aids the attack.

This is a side that is set up to win the ball back as quickly as possible, and Rodri was the main instigator in New Jersey he terrorised the Argentina midfield, sweeping up every loose ball.

His team-mates certainly contributed too, with none of the Argentina midfield able to get a sniff in possession as Fabian Ruiz, Dani Olmo and the back four also carried out beautifully co-ordinated their counter-pressing.

open image in gallery It was dejection for Argentina as they were unable to impose themselves on a one-sided game ( PA )

It meant that Argentina were stifled in what was a lesson in how to nullify opposition attackers, with even Messi struggling as Julian Alvarez, Nico Gonzalez, Alexis Mac Allister and Fernandez were unable to get into the game in forward areas. Spain were not threatened once in normal time, and were barely troubled in extra time either.

And while De la Fuente could have been unhappy with a lack of clear-cut chances for his side at one point, Argentina’s defensive display seemed to just be delaying the inevitable, and the Fernandez red card made a likely win feel like a certain one, even if it did require Torres to deliver the finishing blow.

In the end, it was a near-perfect display from La Roja as they won a second World Cup, with the country’s pre-eminent footballing ideal once again serving as a platform for success on both the European and world stages, as it did between 2008 and 2012. Since then, many teams have tried to imitate that great side. In blending it ideas with his own, De la Fuente has taken Spain to the promised lance once more.
