The Philippines on Monday accused Chinese coast guard personnel of striking one of its sailors on the head with a wooden baton during an encounter in the South China Sea, an incident its defence ministry described as part of a "clear pattern of provocative and hostile behaviour" by Beijing.

The sailor was injured and a rubber boat of the Philippine navy was damaged in the incident at Second Thomas ⁠Shoal, the military said in a statement.

A Chinese coast guard rigid-hull inflatable boat with eight personnel approached its grounded warship on Second Thomas Shoal and took photos and videos, the Philippine military said.

When two Philippine navy boats moved to drive ​the ⁠Chinese vessel away, the personnel "reacted violently and ‌aggressively by striking Philippine navy personnel with a wooden baton".

The Philippine military released a 25-second video clip showing the alleged encounter.

The Philippine military called on the People's Liberation Army and the Chinese coast guard “to put a stop to their illegal, coercive, aggressive and deceptive actions within the West Philippine ⁠Sea”.

Asean ministers are gathering in Manila this week for high-level meetings. Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi is due to be in attendance and tensions in the South China Sea are expected to be discussed.

Manila's foreign ministry said the "act of violence" against its navy personnel was "unacceptable" and warranted diplomatic action.

The Second Thomas Shoal is within the 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone of the Philippines and about 1,300km from mainland China, which refers to it as the Renai Reef.

A pilot reads out a radio challenge against Chinese vessels from aboard a Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources plane in Scarborough Shoal, South China Sea ( Getty )

The Philippines routinely accuses China of disrupting resupply missions to troops on the ‌grounded vessel. A June 2024 incident at the shoal had turned ⁠violent and resulted in a Filipino sailor losing a finger.

The confrontation later led to a provisional understanding with China to allow resupply missions to the grounded ship.

China denies allegations of aggressive conduct ‌during encounters in the South China ​Sea and accuses the Philippines of trespassing ‌in its waters.

The Chinese embassy in Manila and China's defence ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The world's biggest jackpot game, Powerball, is set to be launched in the UK this week.

The National Lottery's version of the game will see UK players compete with their American counterparts to win shared jackpots potentially worth billions.

Operator Allwyn has confirmed players will be able to buy into the game from tomorrow ahead of the opening draw on Thursday.

What is Powerball?

Founded in the US in 1992, Powerball is the world's biggest rolling jackpot game ( PA Wire )

The game invites players to select five white numbers from 1 to 69, and one red ‘Powerball’ number from 1 to 26. To win the jackpot, players must match all six drawn numbers.

In Powerball, the jackpot grows until it is won, which is what allows the winning sum to reach such high figures.

Powerball created the world's biggest-ever lottery winner of $2.04 billion in 2022 (£1.5bn). Edwin Castro, the winner, bought his ticket in Altadena, California.

Winners can choose to receive their winnings over 30 annual payments, but Castro chose the lump sum, receiving $997.6m (£740m) — or $628.5m (£466m) after taxes.

How will the UK version work?

Here, UK players must pay £4 per line to compete with their American counterparts.

The game will offer players uncapped jackpots starting at £12 million.

The UK game features an extra 'match two main numbers' prize tier, which is only available to UK players and offers a fixed prize of £8.

The 'match five main numbers' tier will also offer a fixed prize of £1 million.

All other UK prize tiers will vary depending on the balls drawn and the number of winners.

What is the current Powerball jackpot?

The Powerball jackpot is currently estimated at $544million (£311million), with a 'cash value' of $241.6million.

The latter is the amount, which you win as a lump sum, which is always lower because it has not been invested to grow over 30 years.

What are the odds of the winning?

The odds of winning the Powerball jackpot are 1 in 292 million, according to the operator.

For the other prize tiers, the odds significantly vary.

What will be the weekly timings?

From tomorrow, tickets will be available to buy online or in UK stores until 11.55pm the night before the draws (on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays).

Draws are then set to take place at around 4am the following morning — on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays — at the Powerball studio in Florida.

Argentina could face additional disciplinary proceedings following the brawl that marred the end of their World Cup final defeat to Spain.

Leandro Paredes was sent off after the final whistle after clashing with Spain’s Eric Garcia and Gavi while Nahuel Molina appeared to take a swing at Spain captain Rodri.

Fifa will investigate the post-match scenes before deciding whether to take additional disciplinary action, while sanctions could also follow Argentina’s semi-final win over England.

open image in gallery Leandro Paredes clashes with Spain's Gavi next to assistant coach Walter Samuel ( Reuters )

After beating England, several Argentina players wave a banner that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates to “The Falkland Islands are Argentinian”.

A Fifa spokesperson said after the semi-final, “As is standard procedure, Fifa’s independent Disciplinary Committee is currently assessing the match reports and considering the relevant circumstances before deciding on potential further steps based on the Fifa Disciplinary Code.”

The same process will apply to the final. Argentina’s Paredes and Enzo Fernandez, who was sent off in normal time for two bookable offences, will each receive a one-match ban following their red cards, to be applied in Argentina’s next competitive match.

But Fifa’s Disciplinary Code states players sent off for violent conduct will be suspended for “at least three matches”. Misconduct relating to assault, including “elbowing, punching, kicking, biting, spitting at or hitting an opponent” will result in a suspension of “at least three matches or an appropriate period of time”. Sanctions can also be applied retrospectively.

Luis Suarez is perhaps the most infamous example of a retrospective punishment at the World Cup, with the Uruguay striker handed a nine-match international ban and four-month ban from all football-related activity after biting Italy’s Giorgio Chiellini during the group stages of the 2014 tournament.

France legend Zinedine Zidane was handed a three-match ban following his headbutt on Italy’s Marco Materazzi during the 2006 World Cup final, while Materazzi received a two-match suspension for provoking the Frenchman. Zidane’s ban was never enforced, though, because he retired after the World Cup.

On the scale of violent conduct, Paredes and Molina’s actions at the end of the 2026 final were perhaps not as severe as those two infamous cases of bad behavior, but there is scope for Fifa to increase the punishment beyond the nominal three-match ban. Molina would have to be cited, too, as he was did not receive a card from the referee on the pitch.

open image in gallery Leandro Paredes (right) was sent off following the final whistle ( PA )

Argentina’s football federation could also face disciplinary action, should Fifa find more instances of misconduct during their investigation. Fifa’s code states that “if a national team conducts itself improperly (for example, if individual disciplinary sanctions are imposed by the referee on five or more players during a match), disciplinary measures may also be taken against the association concerned”.

More generally, Argentina’s actions following the final whistle could be seen as “behaving in a way that brings the sport of football and/or Fifa into disrepute”, which may also open the door to additional disciplinary measures.

The post-match brawl was sparked when Spain’s Mikel Oyarzabal and Rodri sprinted past Molina after the final whistle was blown and La Roja were crowned champions. Molina appeared to swing at Rodri, leading to the Spain captain stopping in his tracks and approaching the Argentina defender while shouting.

Molina then squared up to Rodri and bumped him in the chest, which was the flashpoint that triggered Garcia to step in. Paredes, who was booked during the final and was fortunate to not receive a second yellow card, then flew towards Garcia, knocking him to the ground.

Paredes then jabbed Garcia in the throat after the Spain defender got to his feet, just as Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni approached, wagging his finger and trying to break up the scuffles. With Scaloni separating Garcia and other Argentina coaching staff members getting involved, Paredes then turned his attention to Spain’s 21-year-old midfielder Gavi.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Paredes, 32, spun Gavi to the ground and appeared to push into his face while holding him by the bib. Several of Gavi’s Spanish team-mates then stepped in to shield him, with Spain’s Borja Iglesias crashing into Paredes. Video footage also appeared to show Argentina assistant coach Daniel Ayala striking Spain midfielder Dani Olmo.

It was a sorry way for Argentina’s tournament to end after they had taken an emotional path to the final. They were attempting to a second World Cup in a row for captain Lionel Messi, who was playing on the World Cup stage for the final time.

Downing Street called for an investigation into Argentina’s celebrations following the 2-1 win over England in the semi-finals. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) was previously fined £20,000 by Fifa in 2014 after Argentina’s players held up a banner with the same message.

Two years ago, Rodri and Spain team-mate Alvaro Morata were handed one-match bans for chanting “Gibraltar es Espanol” – Gibraltar is Spanish – following their Euro 2024 final victory over England, leading to a complaint from the Gibraltar Football Association.

Broadcaster and journalist Edward Stourton has died aged 68, the BBC has announced.

Mr Stourton’s career spanned more than 40 years, including 10 years fronting the broadcaster’s prestigious Radio 4 Today programme.

He was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2014, but continued to work until recently.

The BBC said that he died on Saturday, surrounded by his family.

Jonathan Munro, the interim chief executive of BBC News and Current Affairs – who also worked as Stourton’s producer when he was ITN’s diplomatic editor – said it was “far too soon to lose Ed”.

open image in gallery ‘He leaves a huge gap’: Stourton worked for many flagship BBC programmes, including ‘Today’ and the ‘World at One’ ( Justin Sutcliffe )

Speaking about his time on ITN, Munro described his late colleague as “unflappable then and ever after”.

“Many years later, I was listening to his superb analysis of the new Pope for the BBC – another of his many areas of expertise. Not many broadcasters can present Today, BBC One’s One O’Clock News, The World At One and Sunday – but he did. He leaves a huge gap.”

Mohit Bakaya, controller of BBC Radio 4, said: “Ed was an absolutely outstanding broadcaster. He brought intelligence, authority and an extraordinary hinterland to everything he did.

open image in gallery The veteran newsreader, top left, died on Saturday ‘surrounded by his family’ ( PA )

“When Ed was behind the mic, whether on Sunday or the various news programmes he regularly presented for Radio 4, you felt you understood the world that little bit better. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this sad time.”

Mr Stourton was born in Nigeria and was one of the founding members of the Channel 4 news team when it was formed in 1982.

Starting out as a scriptwriter, he went on to cover foreign news at the broadcaster, also enjoying a stint as Washington correspondent, where he reported on the final years of Ronald Reagan’s presidency.

He then went on to join the BBC in 1988 before returning to ITN two years later as diplomatic editor, reporting from around the world including Baghdad during the Gulf War, Bosnia during the siege of Sarajevo and from Moscow in the final days of the Soviet Union.

Stourton went back the BBC in 1993 and fronted the One O’Clock News for six years and presented his own Radio 4 phone-in programme, Call Ed Stourton, before joining the Today programme in 1999.

open image in gallery Stourton was a journalist and broadcaster for more than 40 years ( BBC )

He fronted the flagship current affairs programme for a decade, until it was announced in December 2008 that he was set to be replaced by Justin Webb. The decision – which was communicated to him through a journalist before he was officially informed of his departure – prompted a huge public outcry. Two members of parliament, Jeremy Hunt and Keith Vaz, even put forward an early-day motion in the Commons, signed by 90 MPs.

The campaign in support of him ultimately led to the BBC retaining him as a contributor, shifting from presenting work to foreign reporting.

Recalling the time in his 2023 memoir Confessions, Mr Stourton wrote: “The letters that piled high in my pigeonhole were personally heartening, and a reminder that friendships endure even in the febrile world of journalism.”

Mr Stourton also worked as BBC Two’s world affairs strand correspondent and presented editions of Panorama, as well as a series of Radio 4 programmes including The World At One, The World This Weekend and Analysis.

Along with his four-decade-long career as a broadcaster, he authored a number of books, including 2013’s Cruel Crossing and his memoir – in which he revealed he had been diagnosed with prostate cancer nearly a decade earlier.

His most recent book, Made In America (2025), explores US history and how it has led to the era of Donald Trump. It was written to coincide with the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

Mr Stourton is survived by his wife Fiona and his four children.

With Andy Burnham set to finally enter No 10, all eyes are on what his top team could look like – but the contest over who will be his next chancellor is hotting up.

The former Greater Manchester Mayor’s premiership was cemented this week when he was confirmed as the new Labour leader on Friday after receiving nominations from 379 of the 403 Labour MPs.

The former mayor nearly enjoyed a clean sweep of declared nominations, had it not been for backbencher Neil Coyle selecting ex-minister Catherine West, who pulled back from mounting an unlikely leadership challenge against Sir Keir in May.

Mr Burnham, who was sworn in as an MP last month, is facing demands from both inside and outside the Labour Party to generate real change when he enters Number 10.

This doesn’t just mean changes to policy, but also changes to the cabinet – with Mr Burnham likely to choose a team that reflects a broader range of views from within the party than the narrow one represented by Sir Keir Starmer’s cabinet.

Mr Burnham would, of course, have close allies whom he would want to reward with top jobs. But when he gets to the point of naming his cabinet, it will be one role more than any other that will shape his government – his pick as chancellor.

Here, The Independent looks at who might be in the running for his top team.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham will need to pick a top team ( Getty )

Who will be Burnham’s chancellor when he becomes prime minister?

After the prime minister, the role of chancellor is the most important role in government and Mr Burnham’s pick will be the biggest sign of a change of direction from Sir Keir.

While Rachel Reeves gave her backing to the MP for Makerfield in what was seen as a last-ditch attempt to keep her job, it looks almost certain that she will be ousted from the Treasury – and potentially out of government altogether.

There is a suggestion she could land the defence secretary job where she would have to persuade her old department to provide the money to fill the £4.7bn black hole she left in the Defence Improvement Plan.

Along with her would go her economic policy and perhaps her tight borrowing rules – although Mr Burnham has already said he will stick by them.

There are now two names being widely discussed to be Mr Burnham’s prospective chancellor – Shabana Mahmood and Ed Miliband.

open image in gallery Wes Streeting is said to have had talks ( PA )

These names represent very different approaches to the economy, with Ms Mahmood on the right of the party, and Mr Miliband a leading figure on the soft left.

Shabana Mahmood

Most people now expect Ms Mahmood to land the job.

After weeks of wrangling, Ms Mahmood is now the frontrunner for the job. She is seen to be deeply competent after having gained a reputation as a tough home secretary. In an added bonus, her appointment would also allow Mr Burnham to get her out the Home Office and tweak her immigration policy.

The appointment of Ms Mahmood, who comes from the Labour right, would calm market jitters amid concerns that Mr Burnham in No 10 could unleash more borrowing. However, she has not previously held any economic roles as a minister.

But, as revealed by The Independent, there are concerns on the left that she is in favour of cutting taxes and welfare.

Ed Miliband

Mr Miliband had been hankering for the chancellor job for some time and was a leading contender who would overhaul economic policy in a leftward direction. But he is set to be disappointed.

He is now expected to be foreign secretary instead with a brief to reform the Foreign Office and also look at a roadmap back to 0.7 per cent of GDP spent on international aid.

Mr Miliband’s history of taking a hard-line approach to net zero policies have made him a controversial figure, and it is an image that will be hard to shake off.

More female MPs could be brought into cabinet

A number of female MPs would likely play key roles in a Mr Burnham cabinet.

Top of that list is Louise Haigh, who was forced out of Sir Keir’s cabinet as transport minister over revelations of past criminal convictions involving fraud regarding mobile phones.

She has revived her career – not least as a pivotal figure in Mr Burnham’s campaign coordinating his push in Makerfield and wider bid to be the new Labour leader. If Mr Burnham becomes PM, she is expected to get the key coordination role of Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster running the Cabinet Office, the engine of government.

Allies of Ms Haigh have told The Independent that she is set to be appointed the new chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster – running the Cabinet Office and working closely with the prime minister and Downing Street.

open image in gallery Louise Haigh is a key part of Burnham’s team ( Getty )

Another key figure in his campaign was Knowsley MP Anneliese Midgley, who would get a plum role, possibly in as party chair.

Angela Rayner, the former deputy prime minister, is also poised for a comeback. She has quietly put aside her own leadership ambitions to back Mr Burnham. She was forced to resign over her tax affairs but now is looking at a top job, and is being talked of as the next health secretary.

Mr Burnham’s ally and party deputy leader Lucy Powell would also likely get a cabinet post and is expected to end up as deputy prime minister. She is also poised to replace Steve Reed running local government, housing and communities.

The current culture secretary Lisa Nandy would be set for a promotion – she too will be eyeing education.

There is speculation that the current foreign secretary Yvette Cooper could get her previous job as home secretary back, although John Healey, who quit as defence secretary in protest over funding shortfalls, is another name linked to this role.

A third name to look out for as a possible home secretary is Wes Streeting, who resigned as health secretary from Starmer’s government in the hopes of launching his own leadership bid, which never materialised.

Listen to the newest episode of In The Room here:

For Westminster gossip, intrigue and behind-the-scenes insight, 

Who would be out?

There is a chance of wholesale change, which means some surprising figures could be out. Deputy prime minister David Lammy, a close ally of Sir Keir, is widely expected to find himself on the backbenches.

There is also speculation that Mr Burnham would move on from the Morgan McSweeney allies – housing secretary Steve Reed, chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster Darren Jones, business secretary Peter Kyle.

Meanwhile, tech secretary Liz Kendall – who failed previously in the welfare job – is unlikely to land a role in any Burnham cabinet. There is talk that Pat McFadden will remain as work and pensions secretary.

One thing, though, that is always true about new cabinet selections is that there are always surprise names which emerge.

News.title: Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine thuggery
News.content:
Spain should have won far more comfortably, but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world, having beaten the favourites France in the last four.

Spain won this tournament for the second time, 16 years after the first. Now there is just one nation chasing a “second star”, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own, rather than Manchester City signing Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal with Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to to their system. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri, but cherish whoever that is.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: Records tumble at Lord’s as England win thriller against India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 192-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: From the best fans to star players, and the worst blunders to a shocking moment… SunSport’s World Cup awards REVEALED
Sports.content:
IT’S been the longest and largest World Cup on record.

Just the 104 games, played in 16 stadiums in three countries.



Unprecedented in scale.

But now the dust has settled, with the Final played out last night in the MetLife, Sun Sport brings you our official World Cup awards:



Best player

Only one contender. Even at 39 he single-handedly dragged Argentina to the Final.

The greatest: Lionel Messi.

Best goal

Definitely a few in the mix, moments of genuine quality. But, in the end, our top three were:

1 Sidney Lopes Cabral (Cape Verde v Argentina) – Amazing strike from somewhere in the vicinity of Miami Beach.

2 Vinicius Jr (Brazil v Morocco) – A shimmy, a jink and a finish of pure quality. Brazil’s only highlight.

3 Erling Haaland (Norway v Brazil) – Soaring header after towering above Gabriel. Stay humble.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Best miss that deserved to have been a goal

Michael Olise’s stunning scissor kick from the edge of the box that thumped against the Sweden post in the last 32.

Best save

Australia’s Patrick Beach from Ramy Rabia’s header to earn a shoot-out v Egypt, then he was subbed off and replacement Mathew Ryan didn’t get a hand on any of them.



Worst keeper blunder

USA’s Matt Freeze against Belgium.

Maybe that’s just footballing karma.

Gianni Infantino prize for appearing everywhere

Winner: David Beckham.

Runner-up: Gianni Infantino.

Best Stadium

Plenty of support for the SoFi in Los Angeles and the AT&T in Dallas, as well as the Azteca.



But the stand-out winner was the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in the heart of Atlanta.

Simply gorgeous.

Shame about the other stuff (see below).



Worst stadium

The MetLife.

Sure it must have been great when it was built.

But it’s time to knock it down and erect something worthy of the Big Apple.

Maybe with some shade.

Most hospitable city

All of them. It was an absolute blast.



Thank you, America and Canada (I didn’t go to Mexico).

Best fans (extended stay)

Norway – you will never forget them: Ro!

Best fans (short stay)

Scotland – drank Boston dry with a smile and a stagger.



Best unexpected moment

Curacao briefly equalising against Germany.

Sheer joy

Schadenfreude moment

Germany going out on penalties against Paraguay.

Come on, you HAD to enjoy that.

Biggest disappointment

Thomas Tuchel deciding defence was the best form of defence against Argentina.



It wasn’t.

Biggest disappointment (non-England)

Portugal, closely followed by Uruguay.

Best off-pitch surprise

That Americans can get into “soccer” if they realise how important it is.

Every bar TV screen had the games on (and I went into a lot of bars…..) and the locals wanted to hear about the matches and the stars

Best match

Just for the drama of it, Portugal 2 Croatia 1.



A second half with four disallowed goals, a VAR penalty, countless chances and utter chaos at the end. Closely followed by the heroic Alamo stand in the Azteca.

Shame England tried to repeat it.

Worst match

England 0 Ghana 0.



Long journey out to the middle of nowhere to watch a game that nearly died of shame

Best lookalike

Clement Turpin (French ref) /Leandro Trossard (Belgium).

Biggest off-pitch gripe

Realising that when things don’t go as planned, the USA has more Jobsworths per square foot than any other nation on earth.

What happened to showing initiative?

Most maddening experience

Spending an hour to get into the Mercedes Benz Stadium for the England v Argentina semi-final because there was only one security scanner and they then ran out of bag tags.



Swiftly followed by no working WiFi inside.

Apologies for those who read my first edition report.

Shameful moment

Fifa bowing to the demands from the White House to overturn Folarin Balogun’s red card ban.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Utterly disgraceful.

What’s the point in having rules if you can ignore them when your mate picks up the blower?

Sports.title: Who is hosting Euro 2028 and will they gain automatic qualification? Stadiums, full schedule and dates
Sports.content:
ENGLAND fans are hurting after the Three Lions’ World Cup semi-final exit in North America.

But the football calendar moves quickly, and attention is already turning to the next major tournament.

Focus is shifting to Euro 2028, a tournament that will bring the continent’s elite right to our doorstep.



It may be two years off, but it promises to be a huge summer of football on home soil, with planning already well underway.



Where is Euro 2028 being held?

British fans won’t have to travel far to catch the action of Euro 2028 live and in person.

Although first pitched as a five-nation tournament, Euro 2028 will be hosted by four countries – England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland.

Northern Ireland was set to host, but has since lost its status after Belfast‘s Casement Park was dropped as a venue due to redevelopment delays and significant funding shortfalls.

A new total of nine stadiums across eight cities will be used.

England leads the way with six venues, with Scotland, Wales, and Ireland each providing one of their own.

London will supply Wembley Stadium and the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, while Manchester’s Etihad Stadium and Newcastle’s St James’ Park are also locked in.

Villa Park in Birmingham will welcome fans following planned renovations, and Everton’s state-of-the-art new stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock completes the English line-up.



Outside of England, matches will be played at Hampden Park in Glasgow, Dublin’s Aviva Stadium, and Cardiff’s Principality Stadium.

Wembley Stadium (London) – Capacity: 90,000

(London) – Capacity: 90,000 Principality Stadium (National Stadium of Wales, Cardiff) – Capacity: 73,931

(National Stadium of Wales, Cardiff) – Capacity: 73,931 Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (London) – Capacity: 62,850

(London) – Capacity: 62,850 Etihad Stadium (Manchester) – Capacity: 61,470

(Manchester) – Capacity: 61,470 Hill Dickinson Stadium (Everton Stadium, Liverpool) – Capacity: 52,769

(Everton Stadium, Liverpool) – Capacity: 52,769 St James’ Park (Newcastle) – Capacity: 52,264

(Newcastle) – Capacity: 52,264 Villa Park (Birmingham) – Capacity: 50,000 (following planned expansion)

(Birmingham) – Capacity: 50,000 (following planned expansion) Hampden Park (Glasgow) – Capacity: 51,866

(Glasgow) – Capacity: 51,866 Aviva Stadium (Dublin Arena, Dublin) – Capacity: 51,711

Will the host nations qualify automatically?

Because there are multiple co-hosts, UEFA can’t simply hand out automatic passes to everyone without altering the tournament’s competitive balance.

Instead, a unique safety net system has been devised.

UEFA has guaranteed that at least two of the host nations will qualify for the tournament.



England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will all have to navigate the standard European Qualifiers, but UEFA has put two automatic spots in reserve.

If any of the hosts fail to qualify on merit, the two with the highest qualifying ranking will scoop up these backup spots.

It means that even in a worst-case scenario where everyone struggles in qualifying, the two highest-ranked nations are still guaranteed a place.

The qualifying group stage matches will kick off in March 2027, and will be played throughout the year, wrapping up in November 2027.

There will then be a round of high-stakes play-offs in March 2028 to decide the last remaining spots.



Teams will have to wait until Sunday, December 6, 2026, for the official group stage draw.

As for Northern Ireland, their drop-out from hosting duties means they lose the safety-net privilege.

They must now qualify through the standard European Qualifier route, with no back-door backup plan.

Interestingly, despite the country losing its match-hosting status, Belfast will still host the qualifying draw at the ICC Belfast venue.

When is Euro 2028?

The tournament will kick off on June 9, 2028, and run for a month until July 9, 2028.



The opening game of Euro 2028 will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

The tournament begins with 24 teams split across six groups, playing a total of 36 matches over a 12-day block until June 21.

Fans can expect daily kick-off times to be set at the UK-friendly slots of 2pm, 5pm, and 8pm.

The tournament then shifts into the Round of 16, which runs from June 24 to June 27, before ramping up again for the quarter-finals on June 30 and July 1.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Each of the four nations will host one quarter-final match, before the tournament moves to London, with both semi-finals taking place under the Wembley arch on July 4 and July 5.



The Euro 2028 final is then scheduled for Sunday, July 9, 2028 at Wembley.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Mikel Merino hilariously copies infamous Donald Trump dance move moments before Spain lift World Cup trophy
Sports.content:
SPAIN star Mikel Merino performed a hilarious rendition of Donald Trump’s dance move after the president handed over the World Cup trophy.

Trump originally went viral for pulling out the moves to YMCA, but he joined in with the Spanish party on the podium on Sunday night, to Merino’s delight.



After embracing each member of the Spanish team, Trump handed the trophy to Rodri and began to do his viral dance move.

Arsenal man Merino particularly enjoyed the moment and danced along with the president in a brilliant moment.



Fans loved the interaction, as it understandably went viral on social media.

One wrote: “Merino doing the Trump dance has killed me.”

Another said: “Mikel Merino doing the Trump dance right next to him is historic.”

While a third wrote: “Never change, Mikel Merino.”

While Merino saw the funny side of Trump’s antics, Spain striker Borja Iglesias admitted before the game that he would only shake the president’s hand because he didn’t want to “go to prison”.

Ferran Torres‘ extra-time winner was the difference in the clash for football’s biggest prize and Spain came out worthy winners.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Enzo Fernandez’s red card at the end of normal time seemed to put the writing on the wall for Argentina, who had already been under the cosh with 11 men.

Scaloni’s men were unable to keep the persistent Spaniards out and therefore sacrificed their world crown.

And they did it with a whimper, as they recorded their first shot of the whole game in the 117th minute compared to Spain’s 20.

The Argentinians also made headlines immediately after the game as they started a mass brawl.



Boca Juniors man Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the scrap as he went for Gavi.

Anf footage has now emerged of an Argentina coach attacking Spain star Dani Olmo.

Sports.title: Champions League finalist and Argentina coach, 53, punches Dani Olmo in FACE as Spain World Cup final tensions boil over
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA coach Roberto Ayala appeared to throw a punch at Spain’s Dani Olmo after the World Cup final.

Trouble flared after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in New Jersey to lift the trophy, thanks to Ferran Torres’ 106th-minute winner.

The final whistle sparked ugly scenes as players, coaches and backroom staff clashed on the pitch.



Former Valencia defender Ayala, now one of Lionel Scaloni’s assistant coaches, appeared to completely lose his cool as footage on social media showed him swinging an arm towards Olmo’s throat.



Ayala won 115 caps for Argentina and enjoyed a glittering club career with River Plate, Napoli, AC Milan and Valencia.

But the 53-year-old fell from grace after he appeared to catch Olmo around the face before Spain defender Eric Garcia rushed over to drag the pair apart.

Olmo did not appear to hit back as players tried to restore some order.

It was just one of several falshpoints as Argentina’s frustrations boiled over after seeing their World Cup trophy ripped away from them.

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was shown a red card after slamming into Garcia and Gavi, while Nahuel Molina also became involved in a series of confrontations.

Watching on, BBC pundits Wayne Rooney and Joe Hart criticised Argentina’s behaviour, with Hart branding the scenes “disgusting”.

But he was sure to praise Lionel Messi after he was seen congratulating Spain’s players after full-time.

Scaloni also stepped in to try and calm things down before admitting afterwards that Spain deserved to be crowned world champions.

Emotions were running high for the Argentina boss who broke down in tears in his post-match press conference.

The European champions created by far the better chances throughout with the holders spending much of the game trying to break up play.

Enzo Fernandez was sent off moments before extra-time but it was Ferran Torres who finally made Spain’s dominance count in the 106th minute.



He latched on to Nico Williams’ flick-on before drilling a close-range finish past Emi Martinez to seal the win.

The defeat ended Argentina’s hopes of back-to-back titles.

Spain completed a stunning double after following up their European Championship triumph under Luis de la Fuente.

Fifa is expected to review the post-match scenes, including incidents missed by the officials during the chaos.

Sports.title: Man Utd fear after Lisandro Martinez suffers fresh injury blow in World Cup final having missed 92 games in four years
Sports.content:
LISANDRO MARTINEZ appeared to injure himself while committing a foul in Argentina’s World Cup final defeat.

Manchester United defender Martinez was yellow-carded for cynically upending Spain striker Mikel Oyarzabal during an attempted counter-attack in the 41st minute.



A minute-and-a-half later, Martinez was clutching his right thigh having not touched the ball or been involved in any duels.

Martinez then received an awkward pass from goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and touched the ball three more times before he went down in the 43rd minute, roughly two-and-a-half minutes after he fouled Oyarzabal.



Former Ajax defender Martinez collected his runners-up medal and left the MetLife Stadium unaided following Argentina’s fourth World Cup final loss.

United’s medical staff are yet to formulate a plan for Martinez’s recovery and he is now entitled to a mandatory three-week break.



The club are likely to formally welcome back Martinez at their Dublin base for a week-long training camp in August.

United have scheduled their arrival in Ireland for August 8 – exactly three weeks after the World Cup final weekend so all of their internationals are available.

Their first Premier League fixture at Hull City is still more than four weeks away, which offsets the potential lay-off Martinez faces.

Martinez, 28, has suffered several significant lay-offs since he joined United from Ajax in July 2022.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The centre back fractured the metatarsal bone in his right foot against Sevilla in April 2023, which caused him to miss the remainder of that season.

Martinez required corrective surgery on the bone in September of that year and was sidelined for another four months.

The World Cup winner’s return only lasted four games as Martinez sustained a knee injury against West Ham that ruled him out for eight weeks.

Martinez then suffered a calf injury on his return amid another United defensive injury crisis at Brentford in March 2024 and he was absent for six-and-a-half weeks.

Martinez missed only two games in the first half of the 2024/25 season but ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament against Crystal Palace in February 2025. He did not return until November last year.



The Argentina international was unavailable for two months last term with another calf problem and his return ended prematurely as Martinez was sent off against Leeds, triggering a three-match suspension.

Overall, Martinez has missed 92 United matches in four seasons due to injury.

Martinez has played 110 times for United and his contract expires next year, although United are expected to trigger the one-year option.

Sports.title: Lionel Scaloni planning to resign as Argentina manager after leaving World Cup final press conference in tears
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA manager Lionel Scaloni revealed he will “most likely step away” after a heartbreaking World Cup final loss.

The Albiceleste surrendered their world champions’ crown after losing 1-0 to Spain on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.



Scaloni, 48, oversaw a disappointing performance from Lionel Messi and co, who only managed a total of two shots – both off target – throughout the entirety of the 120-minute affair.

The Argentinean tactician, who won the 2018 World Cup and two Copa America honours, was left devastated at full-time.



So much so that the ex-West Ham ace broke down in tears during his post-match press conference when discussing his future as he confirmed he will talk to national team chiefs before his contract runs out in December.

Scaloni said: “I will talk to the president. I have an idea of what I would like to do.



“I will see out my contract and I feel the need, I don’t know if something as big can be done. We need to speak this through.

“I am thankful to the president for bringing me this chance of being in this place where I am at the moment. It was a dream place for everyone.

“We have tried up until the very last minute to give our utmost, the staff and players.

“I believe it’s only fair that I can take this time for myself to think this through…”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Scaloni had to pause as he tried to choke back tears before continuing: “Bear with me, I don’t know if I can continue”.

“This place is wonderful, it is a dream place. We would never have imagined, including my staff, that we would be in this place.

“In order to continue you need a great deal of things, especially resetting your mind, rebooting, creating a group like this again. That is very difficult to create again…”

But Scaloni couldn’t fight back his tears and eventually stood up and apologised before leaving the room.

The Argentina boss said: “It’s really painful, I am very sorry.”



Scaloni then linked up with members of the press at the mixed zone of the NFL stadium.

And the ex-Lazio ace admitted an exit is very possible in December, even though there is still a chance he could change his mind.

Scaloni added: “This place is incredible. It’s everything I ever dreamed of. It’s been a pleasure to be here, a true honor.

“I couldn’t have imagined a better dream. I’ll stay until December, and after that it’ll be difficult. I’ll stay until December, and after that I’ll most likely step away.

“The opinion could change too obviously but I have to speak with the president, and then we’ll see.



“I’ll be eternally grateful to this group and these players. It’ll be very difficult for a group as wonderful as this one to ever come together again, and that hurts me deeply.”

Sports.content:
WHILE the World Cup final saw 22 of the world’s best footballers lock horns, the show was stolen by the star-studded cast of guests in attendance.

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in a one-sided final after Ferran Torres‘ extra-time winner proved to be the difference-maker.



And a host of the world’s biggest stars were present at the New York New Jersey Stadium to watch the final.

Some of the names included footballing royalty and World Cup winners.



A cohort of Spain‘s Class of 2010 were seen in the stands to watch their successors add a second star to La Roja’s chest.

Among them were Andres Iniesta, Xavi, Carles Puyol, Iker Casillas, Jesus Navas and Sergio Ramos.

Fellow World Cup winners Ronaldinho and Ronaldo Nazario, who won the title in 2002 with Brazil, were also seen watching as they featured in the half-time show alongside Madonna.

Footballers Roberto Carlos, Zinedine Zidane, Hristo Stoichkov, Blaise Matuidi, Cafu, Marcelo, Marco Materazzi, Fabio Cannavaro, Robert Lewandowski, John Terry and Fabio Capello were also special guests.



Sir David and Victoria Beckham were once again in the VIP seats at the World Cup as they have been for much of the tournament, while David’s old nemesis Diego Simeone was present to watch his son, Giuliano, star for Argentina.

Sports.title: Man Utd award-winner could be AXED in shock summer transfer despite pre-season heroics as Ratcliffe enforces brutal rule
Sports.content:
IT’S been a summer of midfielders for Manchester United and they will likely let a talented one go.

United fell just short against Wrexham in their friendly opener, but Dan Gore’s standout second half display might still not prevent a summer sale.



Following years of injury frustration, Gore enjoyed a breakout loan spell at Rotherham last season, despite their relegation to League Two.

His intelligent midfield displays ultimately earned him The Millers’ Player of the Year award.



Under contract until 2028 and boasting two successful EFL loan spells after his initial one was cut short through injury, Gore will feel ready for regular first-team football.

On Saturday against the Hollywood high-flyers, the 21-year-old midfielder was technically excellent, spraying the ball about with the confidence of a more experienced No8.



The fact that United controlled possession more in the second half, with a new XI made up of youngsters, was a testament to his efforts.

His season at Rotherham shows Gore is ready for the next step – though whether that happens at Old Trafford remains to be seen.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe has previously complained about United’s inability to generate significant funds through the sale of academy players.

Though determined to impress this summer, breaking into the first team will be tough given the fierce competition for midfield spots among young players.

Sports.title: Boy, 13, dies as Spain's World Cup victory celebrations turn into tragedy
Sports.content:
Boy, 13, dies as Spain's World Cup victory celebrations turn into tragedy

Tragedy has befallen one area of Spain after a young boy died during the nation's World Cup celebrations, when a fountain collapsed as fans took to the streets after victory over Argentina

View 2 Images A boy died in celebrations at the Arbol Gordo fountain (Image: Google Maps)

Celebrations of Spain's World Cup win were marred as a 13-year-old boy died after a fountain collapsed in the north-west of the country. Two other young people were injured, with one child taken to the hospital with a possible broken leg, according to the BBC.

‌



Jubilant supporters were revelling in Los Rojos' extra-time victory over Argentina, as the nation enjoyed their second-ever World Cup win following Ferran Torres' extra-time strike. But tragedy struck at home when the Arbol Gordo fountain in Salamanca's Ciudad Rodrigo partially collapsed.

‌



The Ciudad Rodrigo local police, Salamanca Civil Guard, fire brigade, and Sacyl emergency medical services were called to the scene after receiving an alert in Spain past midnight. People celebrating in the fountain were injured after hundreds of thousands of fans took to the streets across Spain.

‌



The upper part of the fountain's structure is reported to have fallen onto several people, including the 13-year-old who received treatment at Ciudad Rodrigo's health centre before dying.

Mayor of Ciudad Rodrigo, Marcos Iglesias Carisaid: "I couldn't be more dismayed by this tragic news. I join in the grief of the entire family and friends over this loss. What was a day of celebration has turned into a tragedy for all of us in Ciudad de la Mirada. I hope for the swift recovery of the injured. R.I.P."

Three days of mourning will be observed in the city. A statement read: “The City Council of Ciudad Rodrigo expresses its sorrow and condolences over the death of the 13-year-old child.

‌



“The entire city of Ciudad Rodrigo mourns this loss and stands with the child’s family and friends in their grief.

“What should have been a celebration of the Spanish national team’s victory in the World Cup has turned into a tragedy for the entire community of Ciudad Rodrigo.

View 2 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino presented the World Cup trophy to Spain captain Rodri in the US (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

“The City Council also wishes a speedy recovery to the other people who were affected by the incident.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe at centre of heated France rift at World Cup as stunning new details emerge
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe at centre of heated France rift at World Cup as stunning new details emerge

France finished fourth in the World Cup with Didier Deschamps' final game ending in a 6-4 loss to England in the third-place play-off.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe is said to have been involved in some disagreements between the FFF and the France squad. (Image: Eduardo Carmim/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Kylian Mbappe has reportedly been involved in increasing tensions between the France team and the French Football Federation (FFF) in the build-up to the World Cup. Les Bleus went into the tournament as favourites to lift the trophy but came unstuck in the latter stages.

‌



They impressed with their performances in reaching the semi-final. But they fell to a 2-0 loss against eventual champions Spain in the final four.

‌



After announcing that he would leave his role at the end of the World Cup, Didier Deschamps’ final game in charge came in the third-place play-off match vs England. After finding themselves 4-0 down at half time, France almost pulled off an unlikely comeback by making it 4-3, with Mbappe getting a brace, but two further goals from England saw the Three Lions eventually come out as 6-4 winners.

‌



World Cup final LIVE: Fifa investigation demanded after disgraceful Argentina throw punches at Spain players READ MORE :

OIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Following the match, Deschamps hinted at tensions behind the scenes when he outlined the reasons for his decision to step down. “I controlled my departure because I made the decision,” he said.

“I decided it had to end there. And if I made this decision, I say this sincerely, it wasn't for myself. It was for the good of the French national team. I haven't said it until now, but I'll tell you honestly, it wasn't for myself that I made this decision.

‌



“Because the atmosphere was so unbearable, so focused on me, on me. The French national team doesn't deserve that.”

Reports in France have now shed light on a growing rift between the team and the FFF, particularly since the appointment of Philippe Diallo as president. RMC claims that Descamps felt less support from the federation following the change, with Zinedine Zidane now set to replace him.

It is added that there were ‘a few heated exchanges’ between the coach and FFF’s deputy director Erwan Le Prevosr. Issues such as travel, match tickets for families, and bonuses are said to be among them.

‌



Mbappe was reportedly involved in a discussion over bonuses for the World Cup. L'Équipe reports that the squad were told just before their departure for the tournament that they would only receive their bonuses should they reach the semi-final stage.

View 2 Images Didier Deschamps has taken charge of his final France game. (Image: Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Mbappe is said to have stood up and reminded the president in a heated exchange that the players understood the importance of each stage of the competition, while it was his first experience of the tournament. The issue is said to have been resolved on the plane to America, with Mbappe getting his way.

‌



The France captain is also said to have played a role in convincing the federation to install a cryotherapy unit in the training camp. The unit was deemed essential for dealing with the heat in America, but was originally rejected for financial reasons. They changed their minds after Mbappe’s intervention.

As reported by FootMercato , another cause of tension is said to be the €120,000 (£102,000) spent on the FFF officials’ trip to America, compared to how the players’ families were allegedly treated. The situation was said to have fuelled a ‘sense of misunderstanding’ between the team and the federation.

There was also a noticeable absence of any mention of Deschamps in a LinkedIn post from Diallo congratulating the team on making the semi-final. He did, however, post a message thanking the manager following the loss to England.

Article continues below

While it’s still not been confirmed, France legend Zidane looks set to take over from Deschamps as manager. His first games will come in the Nations League when France takes on Turkey, Belgium and Italy in September and early October.

Sports.title: Donald Trump 'scared Spain star s***less' after players were given specific rule to follow
Sports.content:
Donald Trump 'scared Spain star s***less' after players were given specific rule to follow

Spain won the World Cup for only the second time after beating Argentina 1-0 in the final with Donald Trump in attendance to hand out the medals and trophy

View 3 Images Donald Trump made his inevitable appearance as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy (Image: Getty)

World Cup winner Marc Cucurella has previously admitted he was "scared s***less" of Donald Trump during trophy celebrations with Chelsea. The US president was front and centre after the World Cup final, handing out silverware.

‌



Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid this summer, played a key role in Spain's run to Sunday's final, conceding just one goal all tournament. Argentina were unable to break them down in the showpiece too and Luis de la Fuente's side were crowned world champions for only the second time.

‌



However, a lot was made of the production surrounding the match, including a lengthy closing show that delayed kick-off and a half-time performance from a handful of globally recognised artists, which meant the interval lasted almost half an hour. The post-match pleasantries were impacted, with President Trump handing out medals to both Argentina and Spain's players.

‌



Trump also lingered after handing the trophy over to Spanish skipper Rodri, and he awkwardly stood on stage next to it as it was being lifted. This incident drew comparison to the 2025 Club World Cup final, after which Cucurella, who has now had two run-ins with Trump, admitted he was scared of the 80-year-old.

Last summer, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain clashed at MetLife Stadium, renamed New York/New Jersey Stadium for the World Cup in North America.

In a shock result, the Blues dismantled the reigning European champions 3-0 courtesy of a Cole Palmer brace and a decisive strike from Joao Pedro, claiming the Club World Cup title.

During the post-match presentation, Trump distributed the winners' medals and trophy, just as he has done at the World Cup final. Yet he lingered amongst the players as they lifted the trophy, leaving stars such as Cole Palmer visibly perplexed.

‌



Spain's Cucurella was among the Chelsea players baffled by Trump's decision to remain right beside captain Reece James as he hoisted the Club World Cup trophy aloft.

The left-back said: "We had been told that, as a rule, Donald Trump would come to present us with the trophy and that we couldn't lift it until he left.

View 3 Images The president was positioned to the side of the celebrations on Sunday (Image: Getty)

"We were all there waiting for him to leave - but the guy didn't want to leave - and on top of that, we looked at him and he said, 'Lift it up, I'll stay here', and so on. I wondered who would say anything to him, you know... I was scared s***less."

The situation played out somewhat differently for Spain following their second world title triumph, as Trump was ultimately guided to the edge of the trophy presentation.

Infantino was compelled to dash across the stage to direct him to relocate, though Trump remained on the podium as Spain's captain Rodri hoisted the trophy.

The BBC avoided a repeat of the controversy from the start of the World Cup by making a change for Sunday's final

View 2 Images Gabby Logan and the BBC showed the full World Cup final half-time show without interruption (Image: Visionhaus, Visionhaus/Getty Images)

The BBC and presenter Gabby Logan managed to avoid further complaints from viewers by showing the entirety of the World Cup final’s half-time show. Logan led BBC One’s coverage of Sunday’s final between Spain and Argentina, with Joe Hart, Micah Richards and Wayne Rooney joining her as pundits.

‌



In the process, the 53-year-old became the first female to present the men’s World Cup showpiece in the BBC’s history. The panel briefly analysed the uneventful first-half before the inaugural World Cup final half-time show began at the MetLife stadium.

‌



While many had expected the A-list roster of performers to inject some excitement after a drab opening 45 minutes, audiences witnessed a bizarre mash-up featuring Madonna, Brazilian icons Ronaldo and Ronaldinho, BTS, the Muppets, Ted Lasso, Justin Bieber and Shakira.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Luckily for Logan, the entire performance was shown on the BBC without any interruption, which allowed her to avoid the same criticism and fan backlash she received at the start of the tournament. The World Cup opening ceremonies had not been shown in full on live television by the BBC, having instead made it available on iPlayer.

Canadian singer Michael Buble was one of the stars who performed at his country’s opening ceremony last month, as all three host nations celebrated their homegrown talent ahead of the first match they staged at the tournament. Buble performed before the opening fixture - a 1-1 draw between Canada and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

‌



However, the BBC interrupted the performance on their own broadcast, opting to dedicate a chunk of airtime to the football itself. Buble fans were left furious that Logan and the pundits spoke over his performance.

The backlash saw fans of the Canadian call her out directly, which she did not respond to. However, Buble himself soon waded into the row, making things even more uncomfortable for Logan.

"The next day, Michael Buble himself, on his personal account to 4.4million people, puts up one of these posts and it's us in the studio talking over him," she explained. "He just left it there, so I replied to him, sent him a DM and said 'really sorry, we did actually put your whole thing up on iPlayer... and I hope you didn't treat it as a mark of disrespect'.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Buble's fans complained (Image: Getty Images)

"Then he sent back a really long, considered message to me, telling me that it's a shame in this age that people just look for the humour in something first. It was a fair point and I came back and said mea culpa, I never broadcast for clicks and likes but maybe I did intentionally lead my pundits somewhere where I felt there would be a bit of humour.

"Then he came back and he said 'Look Gabby, I appreciate you coming back to me, the BBC have always been so supportive of me, please come to a gig - I'm going to be in the UK soon'. So I went from feeling like I was going to have the wrath of Bubles on my back for the rest of my life to feeling like we might be mates."

Article continues below

Sunday’s half-time spectacle certainly split opinion, with Rooney delivering a brutally frank assessment by telling Logan live on air: "I like a lot of them artists but I thought it was cr*p."

FIFA had reportedly promised the half-time break would only be two minutes longer than the usual 15 minutes, but it in fact lasted a whopping 27 minutes and 24 seconds - just two minutes less than the amount of time the ball was in play during the first half.

Sports.title: World Cup final fight: New footage shows cowardly punch that started ugly bust-up
Sports.content:
World Cup final fight: New footage shows cowardly punch that started ugly bust-up

The World Cup final was marred by ugly post-match scenes as both Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes kicked off as Spain celebrated their victory, the latter getting sent off as a result

View Image Nahuel Molina hit Spain midfielder Rodri as he ran past him to celebrate winning the World Cup

New footage has revealed that the angry brawl after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina was started by a petulant punch by Nahuel Molina.

‌



The European side toasted their second title on Sunday evening in New Jersey, Ferran Torres’ extra-time goal seeing off the 2022 champions.

‌



But the post-match celebrations were marred by some shocking scenes as several members of each side clashed. Atletico Madrid defender Molina appeared to be one of the main instigators, while Leandro Paredes was also sent off for lashing out at Eric Garcia and Gavi, the latter left sprawled on the floor.

‌



And new footage from the post-match scenes appear to show what sparked the ugly clashes. As Spain players ran onto the pitch to celebrate with their teammates, Rodri ran by Molina, who appeared to throw out a punch into the midfielder's stomach.

That left the Manchester City man incensed as he turned around to confront the Argentina defender. Many of their respective teammates then piled in including Nicolas Otamendi and Yeremy Pino.

World Cup final LIVE: Fifa investigation demanded after disgraceful Argentina throw punches at Spain players READ MORE :

Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

Paredes then got involved as he attempted to kick Garcia, while he also grabbed him by the throat. He then targeted Gavi in a furious tirade of punches before getting sent off.

‌



Speaking after the shocking scenes, BBC pundit Wayne Rooney said: "Does it surprise you? It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this with Argentina before.

“It's just not the reaction you want. We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round. That's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's really poor from them."

He added: "That's a reaction to them being outplayed, out-fought, out-thought on the football pitch, and then they resort to that at the end. It's poor from those two players."

‌

Alan Shearer said: “Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone’s face. He went for them. There is no place or space for that.

“We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible.”

Article continues below

Gary Neville also spoke out. He said: “They’re very competitive and I love that element of them, but (Paredes) has just been a disgrace for the last couple of games, and why the referees have allowed him to continue doing what he is doing…”
