3 Football fans wonder whether a 43-year old Messi will be competing at the 2030 World Cup

Each continent will receive a different allocation of places with UEFA (Europe) earning the most with 16.



The Confederation of African football has the second-most with nine, followed by the Asian Football Confederation with eight.

Concacaf and Conmebol both have six places, while the Oceania Football Confederation only have one place.

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino opened the door for an expanded 64-team tournament in 2030.

The proposal for an increase in numbers was put forward in 2025 and Infantino says the success of the expanded 48-team tournament this summer means FIFA should look at a further increase.



"These are all issues that we will be examining after the World Cup," Infantino told Swiss broadcaster Blue Sport.

"When organising a World Cup, it's important to organise it for the whole world - not just Europe and South America, but effectively the entire world. Every nation should be allowed to dream of participating in the World Cup.

"You can see that the quality of the teams is extremely high, and it's getting higher and higher, all over the world. If you don't give smaller countries a chance to participate in the World Cup, they'll lack the incentive to keep improving."

FIFA has also confirmed they will take into consideration that the teams playing in the opening games in South America will need a different match schedule in order to travel, rest and prepare.

Sports.title: Zlatan Ibrahimovic quits Fox broadcasting career live on air in World Cup final bombshell
Sports.content:
Ibrahimovic became a fan favorite in the Fox studio, but he doesn't plan on making a return once the World Cup is done

Zlatan Ibrahimovic is one and done with Fox Sports.

The soccer legend offered a fond farewell to his on-screen colleagues as the network's coverage of the 2026 World Cup concluded from Sunday's final at MetLife Stadium, where Spain beat Argentina to win the trophy.

4 Ibrahimovic appeared to confirm he's leaving Fox Sports after the World Cup Credit: Getty



"I've been talking a lot the last one-and-a-half months, so this will be my last words," he told host Rebecca Lowe, standing alongside fellow analysts Thierry Henry and Alexi Lalas.

"I want to take this moment: Alexi, thank you. Thierry, thank you. Rebecca, thank you.

"It has been an absolute pleasure to share this studio with you guys. You made it very easy for me. I want to thank also, Fox studio.

"I want to thank, America. I want to thank also, all the other people you don't see. I don't remember all their names like Thierry.



"But, you made it easy for me.

"I hope, America, you enjoyed as much as I did. And this is also my farewell to the studio."

When asked by Lowe if he was bidding farewell for good, Zlatan replied: "This was the first and last time for me, so take care, everybody."



Fans react to Zlatan Ibrahimovic's Fox bombshell

Ibrahimovic became Fox's breakout star of the World Cup.

He'd never worked in television before the 2026 tournament, but endeared himself to the US audience as a pregame, halftime and postgame anchor thanks to his bombastic presence, sharp wit and insightful analysis at the desk.

A playful disdain of fellow host Lalas also delighted fans, with many sharing their love for the soccer legend on social media across the last six weeks.



4 Zlatan endeared himself to audiences with a playful disdain of co-host Lalas Credit: Getty

Once Ibrahimovic appeared to confirm he won't be returning to Fox in 2030, plenty of viewers took to X to thank him for his work.

"We are all going to miss Zlatan," one wrote.

"He is a natural. Disappointed he’s not wanting more microphone time," another said.

A third wrote: "Zlatan was the most enjoyable. I actually learned to appreciate soccer listening to him and then went to watch his highlights and learned more about him and the game. It's too bad he's leaving."



"Hell, I don't blame Zlatan. Listening to Alexi Lalas for six straight weeks will drive anyone out of the studio," a fourth joked.

"I fell in love with Zlatan the last five weeks. Absolute gangster," a fifth concluded.

4 Ibrahimovic won't be short of offers should he wish to return to TV Credit: Getty

While its not clear which network will air the 2030 World Cup, with an expensive bidding war expected after the success of this summer's edition, Fox does have the rights to a number of upcoming tournaments.



Both the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup and UEFA Euro 2028 will be shown on Fox.

Ibrahimovic, who won 122 caps for Sweden during his legendary 24 year career, would be a major asset to coverage of the latter tournament.

He played at four European Championships (2004, 2008, 2012, 2016) and scored six goals for his nation.

4 Ibrahimovic would have been a big asset to any Fox coverage of Euro 2028 Credit: Getty



Following a strong studio debut at the World Cup, there will likely be no shortage of networks interested in employing Ibrahimovic moving forward.

Should he wish to make a return one day, he would likely land offers both in the US, and abroad.

Stay up to date on all things World Cup across our talkSPORT platforms - subscribe to our YouTube channel for the latest news, opinion, exclusive interviews and our daily unfiltered, unscripted show 'The S* Word, from 8am ET.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers due for Chelsea medical ahead of £117m move from Aston Villa - as Man United confirm signing of teenage Tottenham winger: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Gomes goes to Villa

Aston Villa have confirmed the signing of Joao Gomes from Wolves. The deal is worth £38m comprised of an initial fee of £34m plus £4m in add-ons.

United land Thompson from Spurs

Manchester United have signed teenage winger Tynan Thompson from Tottenham, subject to the registration, in a deal believed to be worth up to £8million.

It's understood that United will pay £4m plus up to another £4m in add-ons to Spurs who will have a 15 per cent cut of any future sale.

Manchester United have signed Tynan Thompson from Tottenham

Thompson, who was on the bench for Tottenham several times last season, scored 13 goals and contributed six assists across Under-18s and Under-21s games, including seven goals in as many UEFA Youth League fixtures.

Thompson was involved in three senior matchday squads for Spurs last season and was on the bench against PSG and Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

United confirmed the deal in a statement, saying: 'Everyone at United would like to welcome Tynan to the club and wish him the very best of luck for the future.'

CHRIS WHEELER

Rogers due for Chelsea medical

Aston Villa midfielder Morgan Rogers is due for his medical at Chelsea today.

Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday that Rogers's former club Middlesbrough will pocket around £20.2million from Morgan Rogers' £117m transfer to Chelsea, which would represent a record sell-on fee in the Premier League.

Morgan Rogers is due to undergo his medical ahead of a move to Chelsea

The ex-Boro midfielder is set for a move to Stamford Bridge after Chelsea struck a verbal agreement with Aston Villa, after Arsenal had failed to back up their interest with a suitable bid.

When Boro agreed to sell him to Aston Villa, in February 2024, for £16m, they inserted a 20 per cent sell-on clause on any profit generated from a future transfer in the England international's contract.

Diop discussing Portman Road switch

Fulham defender Issa Diop is in talks over an £8.5million move to Ipswich.

The 29-year-old played for Morocco at the World Cup and is discussing a four-year contract with Gary O'Neil's side.

Sports.title: World Cup fans brand FIFA's first-ever halftime show a 'disaster' as Madonna and Bieber's bizarre spectacle divides billions
Sports.content:
Have you got a story? Email tips@dailymail.com

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup fans branded FIFA's controversial first-ever World Cup halftime show starring Madonna and Justin Bieber a 'disaster' on Sunday - as the spectacle divided viewers around the world.

Argentina and Spain superstars Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced to share the stage on Sunday at MetLife Stadium as the Super Bowl-inspired performance got underway - before Spain triumphed 1-0 over Argentina in extra time.

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing her 2000 hit Music, accompanied by giddy Brazilian World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho.

The toned music legend was dressed head-to-toe in Saint Laurent, wowing in a pink satin teddy jacket and corset, mini shorts and lace-up boots, paired with stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium.

The unlikely trio then posed up on the grass and smiled at the crowds.

Bieber, 32, made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song, Everything Hallelujah.

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis, playing his manager alter-ego Ted Lasso.

Madonna and Justin Bieber's performances during the controversial first-ever FIFA World Cup halftime show divided fans on Sunday

Justin Bieber made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with only a guitar to sing a World Cup-themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah - leaving fans baffled

Shakira showed off her toned frame as she performed her hit Dai Dai with Burna Boy

The star looked relaxed as he casually walked onto the pitch before belting out his hit track, adding the final line, 'it's the World Cup, Hallelujah' - with fans left baffled by his song choice.

One fan gave the damning verdict, 'What a disaster this halftime show was. Pre-recorded stuff, no collaborations or surprising moments. Where was Madonna at the end? She could have sung a few lines with Shakira... everything was so weird. So much hype for nothing.'

Yet making clear the division, a second viewer wrote, 'I dislike a lot of things that FIFA does... but THAT halftime show was pretty spectacular.'

Another wrote, 'Who was behind the concept for that haltfime show? Chat GPT?'

Other fans wrote, 'Madonna’s performance was the strangest thing ever, especially followed by the Muppets. The rest of the show was decent. I thought JB’s performance was the best of them all.'

'Light, bright, positive energy. We needed that. Really tired of dark and angry performances.

'It seemed like bieber was off the flow but when Shakira came up after - it all made sense!!!'

'It was great! International and diverse, a positive message, family friendly, and soccer legends hanging with Madonna! Ronaldinho and Ronaldo probably couldn't believe it!'

Bieber's downbeat song choice was undoubtedly one of the major talking points of the performance, with one fan writing, 'Justin Bieber was unfortunately the worst part of the World Cup halftime show.'

Another penned, 'Justin Bieber Hallelujah but this was not the right song choice for the half time show.'

A third typed, 'Buzz killer. Totally sucked . Why choose that song that nobody knows . Beyond me ….' while another wrote, 'terrible song choice.'

Others praised Bieber's performance, writing, 'Justin Bieber looked and sounded great at the World Cup halftime show today!

'Glad he's cleaned up his act!

'Best performance. He knows how to switch people’s moods in a second. That’s extremely difficult to do, most performers couldn’t.'

Shakira returned to the World Cup stage as she flaunted her toned abs in a pink and yellow sequined bodysuit to perform her hit Dai Dai, with Burna Boy, while K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite.

Spain eventually triumphed over Argentina 1-0 after a thrilling 30 minutes of extra time - seen with Trump at the trophy ceremony

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing Music, accompanied by giddy World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho

The toned music legend showed off her legs in stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium

The trio posed up on the pitch as Madonna pulled off another flawless performance

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis playing manager Ted Lasso

Fans had vastly differing opinions on the show - one viewer branded the show 'spectacular'

Others blasted the show over pitchy vocals and lipsync allegations

Fans slammed Bieber for his song choice on sport's biggest stage

One fan branded Bieber the 'worst part' of the show

Others praised Bieber's performance as 'so good' and worthy of the Super Bowl

K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite

BTS captivated the crowds as they continued their return to the stage after military training

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, including a cameo from The Muppets

The stadium was lit up with a colorful globe and the world LOVE

[IMG 320833417 noborder /] Fans had wildly differing opinions on the spectacular

Former England star Wayne Rooney savaged the controversial World Cup final halftime show, quipping the best part of it was 'when it finished'

Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'

The show was also blasted by former World Cup England star Wayne Rooney, 41, who joked his favorite part of the show was 'when it finished'.

'To be honest mine was when it finished I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c**p', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going, I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy I like Shakira I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Fans were left in hysterics by Rooney's comment, with one user on X laughing: 'Wayne Rooney on the halftime show actually made me LOL and then 'I like a lot of the artists, but I thought it was c**p'.

While Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final also included a closing ceremony that featured performances and appearances from Post Malone, Tom Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Stars including Cruise, Timothee Chalamet, Kylie Jenner, Matt Damon and Adrien Brody joined the crowds for the final.

Spanish actor Javier Bardem, skiing legend Lindsey Vonn and actress Julia Garner were also in attendance for the FIFA Gold Carpet event ahead of the final.

Tom Cruise flashed a giddy grin as he sauntered through the stadium ahead of his special appearance at the closing ceremony

Matt Damon and Argentinian wife Luciana Barroso looked giddy as they arrived

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

Will Ferrell was in attendance for the huge match

Javier Bardem supported his home country as he walked the FIFA Gold Carpet before the final

Julia Garner was in attendance to support close pal Madonna ahead of her halftime show

Lindsey Vonn looked stylish as she posed up ahead of the game

Brazil legend Ronaldo Nazario attended with wife Celina Locks

England icon John Terry and Argentina legend Diego Simeone were in attendance

Spain triumphed over Messi's Argentina 1-0 - after a fraught second half which saw the teams play into 30 mins of extra time.

Ferran Torres netted the winning goal in the 106th minute - with a devastated Messi watching on as his World Cup career ended in heartbreak.

World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

The game was set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Post Malone performed ahead of the final

Cruise kept his look casual in a black tee and jeans as he posed for selfies with queuing fans, while flanked by bodyguards

The star looked excited ahead of the final

Jon Hamm arrived at MetLife ahead of the ceremony

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini performed Desire

Extra security checks were in place ahead of the attendance of President Trump for the game

Man of the hour and Argentina captain Lionel Messi winked at fans as he arrived for the final - before his team heartbreakingly lost to Spain 1-0

Spain's Ferran Torres netted the winning goal in the 106th minute (top with Eric Garcia)

A devastated Messi was seen looking dejected after losing

Even on the live television coverage, the stadium was bare with a little over an hour until that closing ceremony began.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Argentina were narrow underdogs against Spain, the European champions, despite being the holders after winning the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Sports.title: Is this the real reason why Spain won the World Cup? Marc Cucurella spotted burying a 'lucky' COIN in the pitch in secret act seconds before kick-off in New York
Sports.content:
Is this the real reason why Spain won the World Cup? Marc Cucurella spotted burying a 'lucky' COIN in the pitch in secret act seconds before kick-off in New York

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

2010 World Cup winner Joan Capdevila has revealed the secret ritual that he taught Marc Cucurella to help Spain win their second star as they defeated Argentina on Sunday afternoon.

Capdevila had previously had to beg US president Donald Trump to see if he might be able to help him secure an ESTA visa to help him watch Spain attempt to secure the World Cup.

After successfully securing legal passage to New York to watch the final, Capdevila could then reveal from the stands an important instruction he had shared with the national team ahead of their meeting with Lionel Scaloni's side.

'In 2010, I buried a coin in the grass before starting the match... I've told it millions of times,' Capdevila shared on social media site X. 'I asked (Cucurella) to do the same yesterday...

'Marc, I love you so much. YOU ARE A WORLD CHAMPION!'

Capdevila shared a video of Cucurella appearing to follow his lead, trotting across the turf during the warm-up and checking to see if anyone is watching him.

When the coast is clear, Cucurella bends down and takes the coin out of his sock and appears to dig it into the pitch, before speeding off to rejoin his team-mates.

Marc Cucurella appeared to follow advice given to him by ex-Spain defender Joan Capdevila

The Real Madrid star raised the World Cup trophy on Sunday as one of the tournament's stars

Now 48, Capdevila started all seven games for then-Spanish coach Vicente del Bosque's historic team in 2010.

Remarkably, the former Villarreal star was the only member of Spain's starting lineup for the final who wasn't a member of Real Madrid or Barcelona.

Capdevila had previously shared a message for US Customs and Border Protection, Trump, and Spain's ministry of education, vocational training and sports.

'I NEED HELP @realDonaldTrump,' read Capdevila's social media post. 'They just told me that I can't travel to the final with my kids because my ESTA [Electronic System for Travel Authorization] has been denied.

'Can anyone help me with this?' he asked his followers. 'You have no idea how excited I was to be there with all my 2010 teammates and this team to cheer them on.

'I can't believe they're not letting me into the USA... and that I'll miss a moment like this with my kids who love soccer so much.'

He also pleaded his case to Spanish radio station, COPE, sharing his belief that his ban stemmed from a 2016 match he played in Iran alongside other La Liga legends.

The State Department does issue visa waivers through its ESTA program, which does not permit travel to the US to anyone who has travelled to Iran since March 1, 2011. Anyone who has travelled to Iran since then 'must obtain a visa prior to traveling to the United States.'

After arriving at the MetLife Stadium, Capdevila shared a jubilant post telling his fans: 'NEVER GIVE UP IF YOU WANT SOMETHING, LET'S GO SPAIN! (Spanish flag emoji)'.

Capdevila travelled with his children, who were able to watch Luis de la Fuente's players make history with victory over Lionel Messi and Co.

Spain were forced to toil against a negative Argentina team who registered just two shots over the full 120 minutes, with Ferran Torres eventually grabbing the winning goal in the second-half of extra time.

Capdevila - who won the World Cup with Spain in 2010 - had previously been unable to secure a visa to watch the match

Cucurella - who inked a £60million move from Chelsea to Real Madrid on the eve of the tournament - was one of the standout players during Spain's campaign and admitted that he was looking forward to celebrating the historic win in some style.

Ahead of Sunday's final, Cucurella suggested that he might get his manager's face tattooed on him if Spain were to raise the trophy.

'I don't know (where I will get it tattooed),' he replied when asked about the idea after the final whistle. 'I haven't decided yet.

'I need to think about it, I need to think about where to get it. People will ask me about it too, so it has to be somewhere visible.

'But anyway, we've got a long journey ahead of us now. I hope people will give me some ideas. I'll think it over and then it will be time to get it done.'

Cucurella was also embroiled in some late controversy after Lionel Messi appeared to attempt to get the left back sent off after Argentina went down to 10 men.

As Enzo Fernandez, who received a second yellow card for a headless challenge on Pau Cubarsi, was making his way off the field, Cucurella appeared to touch his mouth as he spoke to Messi.

Messi quickly alerted the referee and attempted to see Cucurella sanctioned under FIFA's new rules which forbid players from covering their mouth during disputes.

As Cucurella was quickly deemed not to be speaking in anger, Messi's protests were soon waved away by both the referee and VAR.

Sports.title: The great World Cup final 'rip-off'! Fans poke fun at offering for supporters who paid $1m for top hospitality tickets
Sports.content:
The great World Cup final 'rip-off'! Fans poke fun at offering for supporters who paid $1m for top hospitality tickets

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A hospitality provider has come under fire for the offering it has provided for supporters at the World Cup final.

Ahead of the tournament's showpiece event, ten fans secured a $1million (£743,640) package through On Location, a company that describes itself as 'the official hospitality partner for the world's premier sports, music, and lifestyle events'.

Yet when photos of the pitch-side seats those ten ticket-holders had at the New York New Jersey Stadium were shared by Sports Business Journal reporter Alex Silverman, many were quick to hit out.

One social media user said: 'All that to sit on a polyester Amazon couch...'

Another added: 'This is the worst thing I've read for a while. I despise so much of this Americanised tournament.'

A further shocked fan quipped: '$1m? For the worst seats? Who the f*** wants to sit there?'

Fans have hit out at the pitch-side seats given to fans who paid $1m for a World Cup final ticket

The fact they were sitting on sofas and facing the sun was one heavily debated issue

An extra user chipped in with: 'Why would someone even pay that much,' before another supporter said: 'Pitch side views are the worst view in every football stadium on the globe. They have all been royally shafted here.'

Meanwhile, with the game starting at 3pm local time and the temperature at around 27 degrees centigrade, the sun was shining.

All of the supporters were subsequently given special sun hats to deal with the conditions, while they appeared to just be sitting on a regular sofa and behind a glass barrier, issues that further attracted the ire of social media users.

One said: '$1 million and it's genuinely a terrible view,' before another said: 'Glad they threw the hat in there for free given the price, wouldn't have been worth it otherwise.'

A third wrote: 'And you get an obstructed view with the photographer standing in front of you the whole game.'

Despite the furore over the quality of seats, it must be noted that the $1million package does reportedly include several other supposed perks for the lucky fans.

The whole experience was said to start on Saturday when the ticket-holders attended a Sports Illustrated party that was hosted by 50 Cent and Diplo.

They were then transported from Manhattan to the New York New Jersey Stadium via helicopter, while other VIP tickets to high profile events and restaurants for after the World Cup final were also thrown in.

Daily Mail Sport contacted On Location for comment.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino heads into Spain's locker room to hand out Super Bowl-style gold rings to World Cup champions
Sports.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino wasted no time in delivering the inaugural Super Bowl-style gold rings to World Cup champions Spain shortly after their dramatic final win.

On Sunday afternoon, Spain triumphed 1-0 over Lionel Messi's Argentina in extra time after a 106th-minute strike from forward Ferran Torres at MetLife Stadium.

Ahead of the final, FIFA had revealed that it had manufactured 'bespoke championship rings', 30 of which will be presented to the winner in New Jersey.

Infantino delivered on his promise almost immediately after the match was over and was pictured handing over one of the rings to Spain captain Rodri.

The FIFA chief was seen inside Spain's locker room alongside the midfielder, who proudly accepted the ring before putting it on and snapping a picture with Infantino.

A number of Spain's stars - including the likes of Lamine Yamal and Pedro Porro - also posed with Infantino as he also provided them with replica World Cup trophies.

FIFA chief Gianni Infantino invaded the Spain locker room to hand out Super Bowl-style rings

Infantino pictured handing Spain captain Rodri one of the inaugural rings after their final win

Infantino, pictured with Lamine Yamal, also distributed replica World Cup trophies to players

A close-up shot of the World Cup rings handed out to Spain's stars on Sunday evening

Before the final, FIFA claimed that the rings will feature an image of the golden World Cup trophy on one side, while the other will be customized after the final to 'reflect the identity of the winning team'. The details for Spain's ring are still unknown.

2,026 rings have been made in total, with 1,996 of those set to be put on sale for fans to purchase, though they are reported to be on sale for $148,000 (£110,000).

Winners' rings are a tradition in American sport. The team which reigns victorious at the Super Bowl each year are presented with typically rose gold diamond rings featuring the phrase 'World Champions'.

FIFA said today: 'One side of the ring proudly features the FIFA World Cup trophy, while the other will be customized to reflect the identity of the winning team.

'Each ring will be individually numbered, custom-fitted and delivered with its own certificate of authenticity.

'Immediately after the final, the captain and head coach of the winning team will receive temporary rings to commemorate the occasion.

'Each of the 30 rings for the winners will then be customized before being officially presented at a later date, ensuring the perfect lifelong fit for an achievement that will echo through eternity.'

Elsewhere on the day, US President Donald Trump took center stage as he awkwardly invaded Spain's iconic trophy lift at the end of the FIFA World Cup final.

FIFA previously released this mock-up of how the World Cup gold rings would look

Spain star Pedro Porro stands alongside Gianni Infantino with his replica World Cup trophy

Spain clinched their second World Cup title after defeating Argentina 1-0 after extra time

There was no fairytale World Cup ending for Lionel Messi who struggled to assert his authority

Shortly after the full-time whistle, the US President made his way down to the field, where he was loudly booed by the crowd before making his way onto the stage alongside FIFA chief Gianni Infantino.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming Spain's players up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The US President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft in East Rutherford.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players - though the President remained.

He stood to the side of the squad as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

There were an estimated 1.5-1.8 billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, where Trump and Infantino took center stage once again.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the duo undoubtedly clear.

US President Donald Trump took center stage as he gatecrashed Spain's World Cup trophy lift

Trump and Infantino stand on stage as gold confetti falls around them after Spain's victory

Prior to the official trophy lift, Trump also handed out silver medals to Argentina's players - including Lionel Messi - after their heartbreaking defeat in New Jersey.

Fans noted that one Argentina star - Tottenham defender Cristian Romero - completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from the FIFA chief before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, Trump also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars; including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball - which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

Sports.title: Argentina set unwanted - and barely believable - record after underwhelming World Cup final defeat
Sports.content:
Argentina suffered a historic embarrassment on football’s biggest stage as they turned in a shockingly toothless display in the World Cup final against Spain.

Expectations were sky-high before kick-off at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, with fans anticipating an explosive performance from the reigning champions.

However, instead, the crowd in East Rutherford was subjected to a staggering lack of attacking ambition from Lionel Scaloni's side, as they fell to a 1-0 defeat on the day.

The underwhelming display saw the holders write their names into the history books for all the wrong reasons by setting an unwanted all-time tournament record.

The defending champions became the first team in history to fail to record a single shot of any kind during the initial 90 minutes of a World Cup final.

Lionel Messi and Julian Alvarez were left utterly isolated upfront, starved of service as the midfield struggled to string passes together or breach the Spanish press.

Argentina failed to record a single shot in 90 minutes during Sunday's World Cup final

Lionel Messi and Co. were defeated 1-0 by Spain after an underwhelming clash in New Jersey

The incredible statistic painted a clear picture of Spain's tactical superiority, with the European champions dominating proceedings at a sunny MetLife Stadium.

They did eventually end their attacking struggles during extra time when Messi powered an effort at goal, only to see it blocked by Spain star Mikel Merino.

Argentina eventually ended the game with two total shots, while Spain had 20.

However, after the game, the final descended into chaos as fights broke out among the two sets of players.

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their 1-0 win against the South Americans.

Ferran Torres scored a 106th-minute winner after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off in the 93rd minute for a desperately poor Argentina side.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win as Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC : 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Sports.title: Spain's World Cup heroes kick-off celebrations en route back HOME after the final whistle - but not before stars enjoy £1K bottle of red wine and cigars in their New York hotel before late-night dash to Madrid!
Sports.content:
Spain wasted no time in jetting out of New York in the immediate aftermath of winning the World Cup with the victory over Argentina on Sunday night.

Luis de La Fuente's side secured a second star for their nation with a dogged victory against a difficult Albiceleste at the MetLife Stadium just across the river from Manhattan.

But after lifting the trophy in front of a full house of their adoring fans, La Roja opted not to ring in their victory with a night of partying in the city that never sleeps.

Instead, Golden Ball winner Rodri got the party started in transit, leading a round of singing on the team bus as the jubilant players sped back to their hotel for a team meal, before moving on to Newark Airport.

Back at the hotel, noted oenophile Marcos Llorente enjoyed a bottle of Chateau Rayas Chateauneuf-du-Pape Reserve 2014 - which costs a festive £1,009 to uncork - in his room with team-mates Ferran Torres and Marc Pubil.

The stars then boarded the Airbus A350-941 waiting for them - clad in their team's livery - and took off shortly after 2am local time.

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of Monday morning

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Join the discussion Should Spain have celebrated more publicly in New York, or was rushing home for a trophy parade the right move?

The reasoning behind flying out immediately after winning the World Cup is thought to be that the team will be welcomed with a trophy parade in Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles - where Real Madrid often host their own celebrations.

After landing at Madrid's Barajas Airport at 1.37pm, the players are believed to be set for just a little downtime, before heading to the picturesque square to kick-off the party on home soil.

According to Spanish outlet La Razon, officials from Madrid have organised a secure welcome for the players that is set to attract thousands of fans as the team travels to Plaza de Cibeles in an open-top bus.

Once on board the flight, Aymeric Laporte was among the players to pose with the World Cup trophy, giving it a tender kiss in his seat as he soaked up the once-in-a-generation feeling.

Spain had previously celebrated on the pitch with their friends and family, with crossover superstars including seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz also joining in on the fun.

Players were draped in flags from their regions in the country as they posed for photos and celebrated with loved ones.

But the show was thoroughly stolen by Spain's unofficial talisman Keyne Yamal - the little brother of teen starlet Lamine.

Dressed in a replica Spain jersey with his brother's No. 19 and his own first name emblazoned on the back, Keyne darted onto the pitch at MetLife Stadium, where he then ran straight into his older brother's arms.

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Lamine Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigal Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Yamal was all too happy to accept a hug from Keyne and quickly lifted his younger brother into the air before gently placing him back down on the field and putting a red 'Lamine' baseball hat on the toddler's head.

And that wasn't the only hat Keyne tried on while roaming around the MetLife pitch on Sunday.

A New Jersey State Trooper couldn't help but remove his cap to briefly share with Keyne, who tried it on before politely returning it to the officer.

Yamal also posed with his girlfriend Ines Garcia in a sweet photo on the pitch, with the influencer sharing it with the caption: 'You did it. Congratulations, my love - you're a world champion'.

Later, Yamal was snapped lighting a large cigar as he waited in a lift at the hotel on his journey home.

As high-spirited as Spain's celebrations were, they came in stark contrast to the ugly scenes on the pitch after the final whistle, when Argentina stars including Leandro Paredes attacked Spanish players Eric Garcia and Rodri.

Paredes throttled Garcia and pushed Barcelona star Gavi to the ground, while Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by.

Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi later complained to DAZN Spain that rival players had been complaining to the media in the build-up to the final.

Argentina players later turned their backs on Spain's trophy lift in their last bitter act following a blue-and-white campaign as noted for its thuggishness as its strong tournament play.

Sports.title: Bitter Argentina players turn their backs to Spain's World Cup trophy lift after violence marred winners' celebrations - as lip-reader reveals what furious star said to winning captain Rodri during brawl
Sports.content:
Argentina’s sulking stars turned their backs on World Cup winners Spain yesterday as the newly crowned champions lifted the trophy.

The South Americans were outplayed by Luis De La Fuente's side in a drab encounter at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, with Lionel Messi and his team-mates unable to disrupt their rivals with the same aggressive, physical tactics that unsettled England in the semi-final.

Barcelona star Ferran Torres bagged the winning goal in extra time to seal Spain's second World Cup triumph – after first winning the trophy in 2010 – leaving Messi, 39, in tears at the final whistle.

The 2022 champions collected their silver medals from FIFA boss Gianni Infantino and US President Donald Trump on the stage but opted not to watch as Spain lifted the trophy – despite it being customary in finals of major tournaments.

Instead, the Argentina players, coaching team and staff walked over to the end where the majority of their fans were sat and turned their backs as their rivals celebrated.

Footage shows Spain players holding the World Cup trophy aloft as gold confetti explodes behind them, with the Argentina team facing the other way.

Argentina's snub came came after the final descended into violence at full time, with a brawl breaking out between the two sides.

Argentina players decided to turn their backs to Spain's World Cup trophy lift on Sunday

The move came after ugly scenes at the end of the game which Spain won 1-0 after extra time

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their victory.

Torres's 106th-minute winner came after Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute following a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsi – which summed up the South Americans' deplorable approach to the game.

At full time, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also hit Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was also involved.

In the aftermath of the ugly brawl, DAZN Spain claimed Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi complained to Rodri about Las Rojas' pre-match comments alluding to officiating concerns ahead of the final.

The South Americans had benefitted from a series of questionable decisions heading into the showpiece event, with the Manchester City midfielder raising concerns before the final.

'You and [Spain team-mate Aymeric] Laporte. Both of you,' he said to Rodri.

Spain shared fears of roughhouse tactics from Argentina, and their concerns came to fruition with Enzo Fernandez sent off for a shocking challenge on Pau Cubarsi

'You spent the time crying and complaining about the referees, my friend. But you shouldn't have spoken before the match, you know that? Didn't you see what he said this week?'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been when they beat England in the semis.

Astonishingly, Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow, despite it being a clear foul, before attempting to get Chelsea team-mate Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his face while talking to Messi.

New laws state that footballers who cover their mouths when speaking to a player from the opposing team must be sent off, but replays showed Cucurella was simply scratching his nose as he spoke to Argentina's captain.

Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off for a second bookable offence in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-gasp free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, with the first of coming in the 117th minute.

Donald Trump took centre stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon

It appeared as though Infantino attempted to usher Trump away – but the President remained where he was

There were an estimated 1.5 to 1.8billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, which saw Trump take centre stage during the trophy lift.

The US President refused to step aside to allow the victorious Spaniards to have their moment in the spotlight.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming Spain's players up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players – though the President remained where he was.

He stood to the side of the team as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the pair undoubtedly clear.

Fans noted that one Argentina star – Tottenham defender Cristian Romero – completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from Infantino before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, the President also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars; including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball – which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

There was a degree of irony in regards to Trump presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, after previously launching a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said. 'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

Wayne Rooney savaged the 2026 World Cup final halftime show as he described the performance as 'c**p' and said the 'best part was when it ended' live on BBC

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, with the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and the Muppets all performing under one roof

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Earlier in the day, Trump and his wife Melania were seen taking in the action inside a packed MetLife Stadium suite – alongside FIFA president Infantino, Canada's prime minister Mark Carney and Mexico's president Claudia Sheinbaum.

Trump also shook hands with Spain's prime minister Pedro Sanchez as Infantino stood beside them.

Spain's Queen Letizia and King Felipe VI also greeted the president. Javier Milei, the president of Argentina, reportedly watched the game from home due to 'superstition,' The New York Times reported.

Trump also waved at the crowd from behind the glass.

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the President's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children. Barron Trump also showed up for the big game.

The World Cup final also saw a bizarre half-time show, with Madonna, Coldplay, Justin Bieber, The Muppets and Shakira performing during the 27-minute interval, which was derided by Wayne Rooney.

'To be honest, mine was when it finished I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c**p', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going, I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy I like Shakira I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Sports.title: World Cup final LIVE: Fifa investigation demanded after disgraceful Argentina throw punches at Spain players
Sports.content:
Spain have been crowned world champions but the behaviour of Argentina at the final whistle has led to calls for Fifa to ban several players - follow all the reaction

Spain are world champions, beating a bad-tempered Argentina 1-0 in New Jersey in the final.

Ferran Torres's extra time winner came after nearly two hours of goalless football at MetLife Stadium and with Argentina reduced to 10 men by Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez getting sent off for two bookable offences.

At the final whistle, a huge brawl kicked off, triggered by Leandro Paredes attacking a number of Spain players including Rodri, Eric Garci and Gavi - with Paredes sent-off for throwing punches and kicking out.

There have been calls for Fifa to "throw the book" at Argentina, who also turned their backs on Spain receiving their medals and lifting the trophy in another poor act of sportsmanship.

Sports.title: Spain vs Argentina referee made two mistakes in chaotic World Cup final as FIFA informed
Sports.content:
Spain vs Argentina referee made two mistakes in chaotic World Cup final as FIFA informed

Spain beat Argentina in the World Cup final and referee Slavko Vincic's performance has been discussed

View 2 Images Slavko Vincic was the referee for the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina (Image: Heuler Andrey/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has identified two errors that referee Slavko Vincic made during the World Cup final. Spain emerged victorious in the final at MetLife Stadium on Sunday night, claiming a 1-0 win after extra time following a goal from Barcelona star Ferran Torres.

‌



There was drama throughout the game, with Argentina star Enzo Fernandez getting sent off for receiving two yellow cards in the closing stages of the 90 minutes.

‌



Leandro Paredes was also shown a red card after the final whistle, following a heated altercation with Spain duo Eric Garcia and Gavi.

‌



Vincic also handed out yellow cards to Lisandro Martinez, Cristian Romero and Alexis Mac Allister, but Scott has argued why the latter should have been cautioned earlier in the game.

Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal exchange after ugly World Cup final caught on camera READ MORE :

Scott believes that Mac Allister should have been booked in the first half, with the Liverpool midfielder not given a yellow card until late in extra time.

“Referee Slavko Vincic adopted a low-key approach to the World Cup final in the first half, but a decision not to show a yellow card to Alexis Mac Allister could have come back to haunt him,” Scott told The Athletic.

‌



“The Liverpool midfielder’s tackle on the halfway line early in the first half was late, involved both feet and could only be described as reckless. The fourth official had the perfect view, and should have been able to describe what he saw in such terms that Vincic would have shown a card.

“Top referees always want their first yellow to be for an offence that no one can dispute, which sometimes leads to borderline tackles being excused early in the match. But Mac Allister crossed the line in the 15th minute and should have been punished.

View 2 Images Referee Slavko Vincic shows a red card to Enzo Fernandez of Argentina (Image: Heuler Andrey/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“Vincic might have regretted his leniency had Mac Allister later committed another yellow-card offence that had a major impact on the game, such as stopping a significant Spain attack.”

Scott also explained that he thinks and Nicolas Tagliafico should also have been booked for a foul in the first half, with Vincic choosing not to caution the Lyon defender.

‌



“Argentina’s Nicolas Tagliafico could easily have received a yellow card when he deliberately brought down Spain’s Lamine Yamal," he added.

"He was saved by the presence nearby of Lisandro Martinez, but the challenge was so unorthodox, clumsy and deliberate that many referees would have cautioned the defender.”

Sports.title: Christopher Bucktin: 'Trump, Muppets and Temu half-time show that exposed World Cup final's Americanisation'
Sports.content:
The World Cup final should be the purest 90 minutes in sport. Instead, FIFA decided the occasion needed improving by turning half-time into the sort of entertainment you might find at a shopping centre opening.

Before Spain could lift the trophy, supporters had to endure a Temu half-time show, Argentina’s attempt to turn football into UFC and Donald Trump behaving as though he had scored the winner, saved a penalty and built the stadium himself. This was the Americanisation of the World Cup in all its bloated glory. Everything had to be louder, longer, shinier and attached to a sponsor. The football itself began to feel like an awkward guest who had turned up without buying a hospitality package.

For weeks, FIFA had already chopped matches apart with hated hydration breaks which arrived at suspiciously perfect moments for broadcasters to milk another herd of cash-cow adverts. Player welfare was the excuse. The advertisers appeared to be the ones in urgent need of refreshment.

View 4 Images Madonna took centre stage during FIFA’s half-time production, which was widely mocked as a bargain-bin attempt to copy the Super Bowl. (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Football’s great appeal is its flow. Pressure builds, momentum swings, and supporters barely dare look away. FIFA studied that magic carefully and decided what it really needed was another opportunity to sell pickup trucks, takeaway pizza and tablets for heartburn caused by the takeaway pizza.

Then the final arrived and gave us the pathetic half-time show, dismissed by Wayne Rooney with the expert verdict: “c**p”. Madonna, Justin Bieber, Ronaldo and Ronaldinho were joined by dancers, choirs, flashing lights and puppets. With Trump waiting in the stands, it was difficult to tell where the Muppets ended, and the presidential party began.

These were global superstars reduced to props in America’s desperate effort to turn the World Cup into the Super Bowl with shin pads. Ronaldo and Ronaldinho once lit up finals through genius. Now they were trapped in a production that appeared to have been organised by sixth-formers using a voucher, a smoke machine and the entire contents of the drama cupboard.

The whole thing was noisy, tacky and painfully pleased with itself. FIFA wanted a cultural moment. It produced a school talent show sponsored by the local vape shop, with Kermit drafted in after reading the script. Worse, the extended interval interfered with the match. Spain had been in the ascendancy, yet their players were left cooling down while FIFA wheeled out pop stars, puppets and enough scenery to delay a Broadway musical.

‌



View 4 Images Wayne Rooney gave FIFA’s show a brutally simple review, dismissing the bloated half-time entertainment as “crap”. (Image: BBC Sport)

Half-time is for treatment, tactical instructions and recovery. It should not last long enough for Trump to finish telling somebody how large his crowd was, how unfair the boos were and why he probably deserved the Golden Boot. When the football resumed, Argentina provided a different form of American entertainment.

Their defeat descended into UFC, which must have thrilled Trump, a man who enjoys sport most when somebody is being punched, and he can stand close enough to appear in the photograph afterwards. Argentina had carried an ugly edge throughout the tournament. They kicked, snarled, surrounded officials and behaved as though intimidation had been drawn on the tactics board beside corners and free-kicks.

FIFA must respond with serious suspensions and fines. The governing body cannot preach respect, plaster the word across every spare advertising board and then suddenly develop poor eyesight when one of the game’s biggest teams treats the final whistle as the opening bell.

‌



Yet even Argentina’s meltdown was not the final indignity. Trump had been badly booed whenever his face appeared on the giant screens. It became the most popular part of the entertainment, and the only audience participation FIFA had not rehearsed for weeks. When he walked out for the presentation, the boos grew louder. Trump wore the frozen grin of a man trying to convince himself that tens of thousands of people were cheering his name in a difficult European accent.

Then Spain lifted the trophy, and he refused to leave. He remained beside the winners like a lodger who had stopped paying rent, eaten everything in the fridge, changed the Wi-Fi password and was now asking whether his relatives could stay until Christmas.

View 4 Images Even Gianni Infantino tried to usher Donald Trump away as the President lingered beside Spain’s victorious players during their World Cup celebrations

Even Gianni Infantino, Trump’s most devoted fan boy, tried to usher him away. Watching the FIFA boss attempt to shift him was like seeing a nervous waiter tell a billionaire that the restaurant closed 45 minutes ago and the chairs were already on the tables. Trump ignored him. He stayed planted beside Spain, grinning at the cameras as though their prize for winning the World Cup was appearing in his latest campaign photograph.

‌



Beside him, Infantino wore white trainers with a suit. He should have been holding a white flag and surrendering his job. Under him, FIFA allowed America to take the world’s game and force it into the shape of its television industry.

Matches were stopped for adverts. Half-time became a concert. Football legends became stage furniture. Players became supporting actors. Trump turned the presentation into a campaign appearance and then had to be encouraged towards the exit like a stubborn uncle at closing time.

Spain supplied the football, the class and the dignity. FIFA supplied the Muppets. Argentina supplied the punches. Trump supplied the boos. Between them all, they turned the beautiful into an ugly spectacle.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker tears into 'crazy' Enzo Fernandez as Argentina star's gesture says it all
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker tears into 'crazy' Enzo Fernandez as Argentina star's gesture says it all

Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the World Cup final after the Argentina and Chelsea midfielder received two yellow cards in the space of 10 minutes against Spain

View 2 Images Gary Lineker

Gary Lineker described Enzo Fernandez’s red card in the World Cup final as 'crazy' - as Alan Shearer branded the Argentina star 'stupid'. Fernandez was sent off just before the additional period for a second yellow card.

The Chelsea midfielder picked up his first yellow card for showing dissent towards referee Slavko Vincic. He received his marching orders after a poor challenge on Pau Cubarsi in the last minute of normal time.

Fernandez raised his hands to the Argentinian supporters, asking for forgiveness as he made his way down the tunnel. And following his side’s 1-0 defeat, Fernandez witnessed his team-mates Leandro Paredes and Thiago Almada clash with Spain’s Gavi, which resulted in Paredes also receiving a red card.

And the chaotic scenes led to Lineker saying on the Rest is Football podcast: “We saw a bit after the final whistle. Paredes let himself down.”

To which Micah Richards replied: “That was embarrassing. Win or lose, you’ve got to shake hands” - before Lineker continued: “Most of their players were magnanimous. Messi and others, they were fine.

“Paredes got given a red card after the game, which is just. Enzo Fernandez, that was crazy wasn’t it? The first one was for whinging.”

Before Shearer weighed in saying: “Absolutely stupid. He got done for dissent which he should never have done. But then to do that…

“To go into that tackle when you’re on a yellow, that’s when you thought Spain are going to win this. He’s cost his country massively. As much as he helped get them through to the final with that wonderful goal against England, he’s cost them.”

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card in the closing stages of normal time

Reflecting on his side’s defeat, Lionel Scaloni said: “I feel sadness but knowing that we left everything out there. I have a lot of things to say about how we got here, but it’s not worth it.

“I want to thank these guys eternally for giving us another World Cup final and for competing until the end. They were better, that’s the truth.

“But I’ll hold on to an enormous memory of what they have done, of what it’s worth to get this far. We have to give it huge validity because it takes a lot to get here.”

Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau wanted Donald Trump's help after controversy at The Open
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau wanted Donald Trump's help after controversy at The Open

Bryson DeChambeau was left fuming that he was handed a two-shot penalty at The Open and as he argued his case called for the assistance of Donald Trump

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau was left fuming after being handed a penalty at The Open (Image: Sky Sports)

Bryson DeChambeau wanted to get Donald Trump involved as he argued strongly against a two-shot penalty following his second round at The Open.

‌



The American was bang in contention heading into the weekend but was called to face the officials on Friday night. They told him that he was to be punished for “inadvertently improving his lie” after landing in the rough on the fifth hole.

‌



DeChambeau requested they go back to the hole where the offence occurred and made his anger known as he engaged with Grant Moir, the R&A’s rules boss. At one point he told Moir: “I just won’t play tomorrow”.

‌



Now it has emerged that, as per journalist and course architect Geoff Shackelford, during discussions with the R&A DeChambeau requested Trump’s involvement. The US President has recently shown a willingness to influence sporting events by helping overturn a red card in the World Cup.

Bryson DeChambeau breaks silence after The Open two-shot penalty amid quit fears READ MORE :

On Saturday, chief executive Mark Darbon was asked if he had received a call from Trump and said: “No. I have not received a call from president Trump, and we’ll see what happens from here.”

‌



Trump recently copped criticism for phoning FIFA boss Gianni Infantino and asking him to review a red card handed to US star Folarin Balogun. It was ultimately suspended, meaning the striker was able to play in America's quarter-final against Belgium. The tournament was ultimately in the US, giving him more leverage than in the UK.

Trump has continued to engage with the R&A in an attempt to persuade them to take the Open back to Turnberry, the links he owns in Ayrshire, which last held the tournament in 2009.

View 2 Images Donald Trump involved himself in decisions that were made in the World Cup (Image: MANDEL NGAN, AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

DeChambeau's antics angered the field and delayed the tee times being announced for the Saturday. Rory McIlroy said: “I think there’s no doubt that he improved the line of his backswing. Whether it was careless or whether it was intentional, I don’t think it matters. Hopefully it was careless but I think the two-shot penalty was justified, for sure.”

He also added on the American's complaints: “I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it is for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

DeChambeau finished in a tie for 14th as he finished on four under par. He carded a 72 on Sunday, meaning he never threatened the leaders.

Sports.title: Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match
Sports.content:
Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match

Argentina enlisted the help of the dark arts in the World Cup final but were architects of their own downfall as Spain lifted the trophy

View 7 Images Argentina have been slammed for their approach to the World Cup final against Spain (Image: Getty)

Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in the World Cup final after taking the game to extra time. But Lionel Scaloni's side once again relied on the dark arts and two of their players saw red.

‌



Spain are world champions once more and Luis de la Fuente's cohort can hold their heads high after their one-goal victory in New Jersey. But the same cannot be said for their opposition.

‌



Much as it was when Argentina clashed with England in the semi-finals, skirmishes, vicious tackles and often embarrassing antics were plentiful during what was meant to be a great display of footballing excellence.

‌



Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez was sent off at the end of the regulation 90 minutes and the villainous Leandro Paredes received a red post-match for throwing punches. We take a look at all 27 of the dirty tricks Argentina attempted against Spain, to no avail.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Alan Shearer calls for major rule change during Spain vs Argentina World Cup final READ MORE :

Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal exchange after ugly World Cup final caught on camera READ MORE :

4 mins

Gonzalo Montiel grabs Alex Baena on the halfway line with the ball overhead and emphatically pleads for a foul. The referee gives it the other way.

‌



6 mins

Alexis Mac Allister pulls Pedro Porro back as he tries to play a one-two on the edge of the Argentina area. No foul given.

8 mins

Nicolas Tagliafico throws himself to the ground after the slightest touch from Lamine Yamal.

14 mins

Mac Allister goes flying in and catches Dani Olmo in an awful tackle. He was lucky not to get a yellow.

‌



View 7 Images Mac Allister went sliding in early (Image: Getty)

19 mins

Cristian Romero ushers Baena out of play and then stares him down as he steps over him in an intimidating manner. This was quickly followed by Fernandez falling to the ground after claiming he was caught from the throw-in.

29 mins

Tagliafico again hauls down Yamal and is basically hanging off his back. No card.

‌



41 mins

Spain attempt to break after winning the ball back but Lisandro Martinez hacks down Mikel Oyarzabal and is shown a yellow card. He was substituted two minutes later.

51 mins

Paredes mindlessly shoulder-charges Rodri in the middle of the pitch with the ball nowhere in sight. He then thuggishly shoves Olmo down and is shown a card amid the ongoing scuffle.

View 7 Images Paredes was shown a card for his jab (Image: Getty)

‌



56 mins

Julian Alvarez goes up for a challenge with Aymeric Laporte and leaves an elbow on him. The Spain star goes down clutching his face.

76 mins

Paredes again, having also committed a foul just outside the box before the hydration break, goes flying into Spain substitute Mikel Merino.

77 mins

Pedri gets a dangerous shot off from just outside the Argentina area but is pushed twice by Alvarez, who puts him off. No foul, but the tactics pay off.

‌



81 mins

Giuliano Simeone chases down a loose ball behind Marc Cucurella and delivers an elbow into the Spain defender's back.

View 7 Images Simeone went flying into Cucurella (Image: Getty)

82 mins

Fernandez wants a foul but doesn't get one so he vents his frustration at the referee and throws his hand in anger. He's booked for dissent.

‌



84 mins

Minutes after being booked, Fernandez drags down Merino as Spain try to break. The Chelsea man then stands in front of the ball, preventing a quick free-kick.

90 + 1 mins

Lionel Messi runs straight into Laporte, knowing exactly what he's doing and drawing a late free-kick in a dangerous area.

90 + 3 mins

The flashpoint of the regulation 90. Fernandez, on a yellow, flies into Pau Cubarsi as the ball is cleared. He sends the Spain defender into a mid-air cartwheel and unbelievably tries to plead his innocence as he's shown a second yellow card and sent off.

‌



View 7 Images Fernandez was sent off (Image: Getty)

90 + 4 mins

To add to Fernandez's disgraceful behaviour, captain Messi enlists the help of his fellow players to try to get Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth whilst speaking. The Real Madrid defender put his fingers to his lips for a split second at most.

90 + 5 mins

Paredes brings down Ferran Torres just outside the Argentina penalty area. Yamal goes close from the resulting free-kick and the game goes to extra time with La Albiceleste yet to have a shot on target.

‌



Extra time - 92 mins

Tagliafico charges into Porro with his elbow extended. He strikes the Spurs man in the jaw.

96 mins

A ball into the Argentina box isn't dealt with and substitute Nico Williams pokes it home. But Nicolas Otamendi had chucked himself into the air and screamed as the cross came in and because Merino ever so slightly stood on his foot, the goal is chalked off. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez stays down afterwards for good measure.

View 7 Images Spain's goal was ruled out because of a foul on Otamendi (Image: Getty)

‌



104 mins

Simeone waits for Cucurella to reach him as a looping through ball is played into Spain's half and goes down yelling. The referee was not buying it, as replays showed Simeone had already leapt like a salmon before Cucurella made contact.

105 mins

Tagliafico and Yamal clash again, this time, all the Argentina players run over to an altercation on the touchline. Manager Scaloni got involved in what was a nothing incident.

105 + 2 mins

Tagliafico is barely touched by Torres as Spain have a throw-in but he collapses to the ground once more.

‌



105 + 3 mins

Paredes again. The midfielder barges into Merino's legs as the Spaniard jumps for the ball in a challenge that could have ended up far worse than it did.

View 7 Images The discredited Paredes made awful challenges in the match and was sent off after it (Image: Getty)

111 mins

Merino is taken out by Mac Allister, who goes into the book more than 100 minutes after he probably should have. Argentina have conceded now and the dirty tactics stop to a degree as they chase the game.

Article continues below

Full time

Spain win the World Cup and Argentina are disgraced in the ensuing celebrations. Paredes is sent off for throwing punches and grappling with Spanish substitute Gavi.

Celebrations

Other players, including Otamendi and Nahuel Molina, also have a pop as what was meant to be an exhibition of the world's finest footballers concludes with La Albiceleste shamed.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney 'speechless' over Gianni Infantino's 'stupid' decision at World Cup final
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney 'speechless' over Gianni Infantino's 'stupid' decision at World Cup final

The FIFA President was joined by the President of the USA as they presented the World Cup trophy to Spain, with BBC pundit and former England striker Wayne Rooney not impressed

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been criticised for his footwear at the World Cup final. (Image: Eva Marie Uzcategui - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney has called Gianni Infantino’s decision to wear trainers with his suit during the World Cup final presentation ‘stupid’. The FIFA president walked onto the pitch alongside US President Donald Trump ahead of presenting Spain with the trophy.

‌



The nation won the title for the second time in their history thanks to a 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina. Spain dominated the match, but couldn’t find a way past Lionel Scaloni’s side in 90 minutes.

‌



Argentina were reduced to 10-men just before full-time of normal time when Enzo Fernandez was shown a second yellow card. Their stubborn resistance was broken by Ferran Torres in the 106th minute.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

World Cup final LIVE: Fifa investigation demanded after disgraceful Argentina throw punches at Spain players READ MORE :

Argentina facing double punishment after 'disgusting' scenes in World Cup final defeat READ MORE :

There was a lot of noise around Trump’s involvement in the trophy presentation, with the President making his way out onto the pitch alongside Infantino. There were some audible jeers as the duo made their way to the middle of the pitch, but it was the FIFA chief’s footwear that caught Rooney’s eye.

As the two walked out, Joe Hart said on BBC’s coverage of the presentation: “Waz’s (Rooney’s) golf partner there.”

‌



The comments get no response from the former England captain, with presenter Gabby Logan saying: “He’s hung you out to dry there.”

Micah Richards added “It’s the first time you’ve been speechless!” Rooney then responded: “I’m speechless at Infantino’s trainers, he talks about everything else, and then he comes. He has to represent FIFA better than that. With those trainers on, it’s stupid.”

Logan added: “That’s half-time entertainment, that’s VAR and trainers with suits, that’s a trio of hate from Wayne Rooney at this World Cup. There’s a few other things that you might want to bring up with it, but his trainers will be on the list.”

‌



View 2 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino presented the World Cup trophy to Spain captain Rodri (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

It’s not only Rooney who had a problem with Infantino’s footwear. Supporters watching the game took to social media to give their thoughts. “You could see Infantino’s trainers from space,” one said.

“Rooney having pop at Infantino’s white trainers, calling them “stupid”. Class,” a second said. “Look, its very much not the worst thing he has done, but Infantino combining a dark grey suit with the whitest trainers in history just reeks of a man out of touch with reality,” a third added.

‌



A fourth said: “Right at the end, Infantino wearing white trainers with his suit is the worst thing that’s happened at the World Cup. Congrats.”

After handing out the medals, both Infantino and Trump presented the World Cup trophy to Spain captain and player of the tournament, Rodri. Despite hints from both the midfielder and Infantino that he should leave the podium, Trump appeared to be keen to hang around for when the trophy was lifted into the air.

He was, however, quickly ushered off stage by the FIFA president shortly after the trophy lift. It’s not the first time something similar has happened with Trump remaining on stage as Chelsea lifted the Club World Cup last summer.
